#4152. Heartopia goes to the movies with its next event

Heartopia's Whale Island will soon host a new event that's all about the magic of cinema.

Heartopia’s next in-game event has been announced, and it’s one you may not have seen coming. Developer XD Games revealed Dreamlight Cinematics Festival, an upcoming limited-time event that celebrates cinema and movie-making.

Dreamlight Cinematics kicks off March 21, and will run through May 1, available across the game’s PC and mobile versions.

Dreamlight Cinematics Festival takes place on Whale Island. And, perhaps as an unofficial Oscars tie-in, it’s all about classic Hollywood filmmaking. Not only that, it also celebrates the aesthetics and industrial design of that era.

All around the game’s world, you’ll be able to find festival-themed collectables, which you can then use to unlock free Time-Limited Exhibition Passes.

If you log in during the event’s runtime, you’ll get the Car Cinema furniture set for free. This cosmetic bundle comes with chairs that are modelled after vintage vehicles, as well as poster display stands with unique movie making-themed decorations.

If you’re looking to spend some money, the Deluxe Festival Pack comes with a large Island Sunset Billboard, which you can place outside your home so everyone knows you spent that money. The same pack also comes with the Popcorn Movie Ticket chat bubble skin, and a 10% bonus to Festival Tokens when you sell stuff at the store.

Regardless of which pack you get, you’ll earn collection points for each, which puts you on the path to unlocking outfits like the Dreamlight Cinematics Festival-specific Modern Show Dandy and Modern Show Belle. There’s also a Cinematic Moments building material set launching with this event.

For now, we have the above reveal trailer to go on, which does offer some idea of what it’s going to look like in-game. Until things kick off on the weekend, you best arm yourself with some Heartopia codes.

#4151. Marvel Cosmic Invasion's Doctor Doom-Themed DLC Gives It The Post-Game Tail It Was Missing

Marvel Cosmic Invasion was a bit of a dream game for me; I loved the X-Men arcade game in the '90s, so when Tribute Games released the excellent Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Shredder's Revenge in 2022, I immediately hoped they'd revitalize other licensed brawler franchises released by Konami in the late '80s and early '90s. While we still haven't heard any word of a new brawler starring The Simpsons, Tribute did follow up its Turtle triumph with Marvel Cosmic Invasion, another throwback side-scrolling beat 'em up, this time starring Marvel's mightiest.

I played through Marvel Cosmic Invasion multiple times and had a blast, but I moved on quickly, as I didn't feel the need to collect different palette-swaps of the many heroes on offer. Even after Cyclops and The Thing joined the roster as DLC in May, I still saw Cosmic Invasion as a game in the rearview. That changes this week, as The Siege of Castle Doom not only adds two additional playable characters (Invisible Woman and Doctor Doom), but also a mode that has the potential to bring me back for more runs for the foreseeable future.

Seeing that Annihilus is threatening the universe, Doom decides to take matters into his own hands. Unfortunately, much in the way that it seems that he may try to fix the multiversal incursions in the upcoming Avengers: Doomsday, Victor Von Doom's solution in Marvel Cosmic Invasion – the Cosmic Inductor – would lead to untold death and destruction. In The Siege of Castle Doom, you select your team and fight your way through various floors of the stronghold belonging to the man who is perhaps Marvel's greatest villain. Your goal is to fight through the winding, randomized hallways of Castle Doomstadt, charging Reed Richards' Stabilizer and tactically bolstering your team along the way, before Doctor Doom can enact his plan.

As for the new playable characters, Doctor Doom is less agile, but his attacks pack a whallop, while Invisible Woman's force fields and speed make her the more versatile pick. I don't know that I see either of them replacing my mains from the base game, but I had fun experimenting with them throughout this mode. Regardless of which character you choose from the expanding roster, you still must traverse Castle Doomstadt before Doom achieves his objective.

Fighting through waves of enemies across differently themed and booby-trapped rooms, you encounter all manner of foes from the base game, as well as new minion types from Doom. When you defeat enemies, they drop batteries that charge your Stabilizer, letting you even the odds and stop Doom. Conversely, each time an enemy hits your character, it charges Doom's Cosmic Inductor, inching him closer to victory and making his minions faster and stronger in the process. As you might expect, the rooms get harder the deeper you go, and while each player starts with two characters to swap between, if a character completely depletes their health, they're gone for good, making it even tougher. As such, you need to keep your eyes on each character's health and swap them out when it makes sense.

As you complete each room, you can choose which path to take to augment your characters with new special abilities. True to the roguelite structure, as you complete rooms, you can also buff your characters' stats within the run. Certain rooms offer extra batteries to help your Stabilizer charge, while others offer new and upgraded equipment. There's also one that promises random events that can easily alter the trajectory of your run for better or worse. Though I often enjoyed boosting attack stats to make enemies less like damage sponges, I had to balance that against buffing their health to keep them alive and charging the Stabilizer to have a fighting chance.

Beyond the in-run upgrades and modifiers, you can also amp up the action run-over-run through upgrades in Reed's Lab, which add to the pool of modifiers you can select from at the start of each run. The expansion also adds new palettes for existing heroes, plus new music by composer Tee Lopes. While I've only done a few runs of The Siege of Castle Doom (each taking between 45 and 90 minutes, depending on how successful you are), I feel a revitalized sense of excitement for Marvel Cosmic Invasion. Tribute claims completionists can spend upwards of 15 hours in this new mode, which has me champing at the bit to dive back into what will likely be my primary way of interacting with Marvel Cosmic Invasion going forward.

Marvel Cosmic Invasion – The Siege of Castle Doom is available today on all platforms, and it is a strong addition to an already great game. You can read our review of the base version of Marvel Cosmic Invasion here.

#4150. Bandai Namco Reveals Its Involvement On Zelda: Ocarina Of Time

Just recently, Xenoblade Chronicles developer Monolith Soft revealed its involvement on Zelda: Ocarina of Time for Switch 2, confirming that it contributed to various aspects including "game design, programming, and graphics".

Monolith's involvement isn't a huge surprise given it's previous work on other Zelda titles, but another company has now spoken up to confirm its own involvement: Bandai Namco.

Taking to its official website, Bandai Namco revealed it helped out with various visual elements of the game ahead of its release on 5th November 2026:

"We were commissioned to create some of the visual assets and artwork, including characters, terrain, animations, cutscenes, and UI, for the Nintendo Switch™ 2 game "The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time," released by Nintendo Co., Ltd. on November 5, 2026."

Of course, the primary developer for Ocarina of Time is Nintendo itself, with Hokwai Ng serving as director, with Eiji Aonuma and Hidemaro Fujibayashi on board as producers. We might be jumping the gun here, but we suspect Fujibayashi-san, who directed both Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom, is likely helming the next mainline game.

In a recent interview, Aonuma-san stated that the reason behind the assignment of HokWai Ng was his ability to "solve problems aggressively". He also presented some interesting ideas for future projects, prompting Aonuma to view him as the ideal candidate to helm Ocarina of Time.

#4149. Harry Potter star Daniel Radcliffe doesn't think he'll watch the show, but wants to meet new Potter Dominic McLaughlin

Original star Daniel Radcliffe wishes the new Harry Potter actor the best of luck

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

25 years after Daniel Radcliffe first brought the young wizard to life in the 2001 movie Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone, the star has wished the new Harry Potter the best of luck ahead of the new TV show adaptation hitting HBO this Christmas.

When asked if he has any advice for new Harry Potter star Dominic McLaughlin, Radcliffe told Associated Press, "I'm really, truly in the business of not giving Dominic advice. He's got it. He doesn’t need any advice from me. If I say something to you, then the next interview people have with him, they’ll be like, 'Oh, Dan said you should do this.' And I don’t want to haunt this poor child through interviews. So I have no advice for him. He's gonna be amazing, and I hope that I will get to meet him someday, and I'm very excited about that."

However, Radcliffe doesn't think he will be tuning into the series. "I don’t know if I will [watch it], honestly," said Radcliffe. "I’ve watched [and] been in a lot of Harry Potter already. Also, I don’t watch any TV. I haven’t seen Breaking Bad. I haven’t seen Mad Men. I haven’t seen some of the real classics. So, you know. Eight hours is a lot of anything to watch."

Radcliffe was just 11 years old when he started filming the first Harry Potter movie, and returned to the franchise almost every year until the eighth and final movie, Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows: Part 2, released in 2001. Radcliffe was 21 years old when he finished playing Potter for good. McLaughlin is in a very similar position. The now 12-year-old has a long road ahead, as HBO plans to shoot seven seasons over 10 years, meaning McLaughlin will also be in his early 20s when filming ends.

Harry Potter season 1, officially titled Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone, will adapt the first book just as the first movie did, following Harry's first year at Hogwarts after he finds out that he is a wizard. But the series format allows the new adaptation to delve into the source material further. With that in mind, McLaughlin arguably has an even harder task than Radcliffe did, having to log so many hours of content.

Alongside McLaughlin, the younger cast also includes Arabella Stanton as Hermione Granger, Alastair Stout as Ron Weasley, and Lox Pratt as Draco Malfoy. As for the adults, John Lithgow plays Dumbledore, Janet McTeer plays Minerva McGonagall, Paapa Essiedu plays Snape, and Nick Frost has been cast as Hagrid.

Harry Potter season 1 hits HBO and HBO Max on Christmas Day. For more, check out our ranking of the Harry Potter movies, and keep up with new TV shows on the way.

It's been a fairly chill week for new releases with ZERO PARADES: Director's Cut the only notable launch (at least in my opinion). Hopefully something from our Deep Discounts sales roundup, or Xbox's Free Play Days titles are worth a shot.

Alrighty then, let's get into it. Here's what we're playing on Xbox this weekend:

I think I'm in need of a nice, feel good weekend of gaming. I'd like to play stuff that leaves me feeling all warm and fuzzy. It's appropriate timing, really, considering just how quickly it's getting dark now that the clocks have changed here in the UK.

Top of the agenda is starting The Wolf Among Us Remastered. I claimed the original version with Games with Gold, yet I've still not managed to boot it. Somehow, I've managed to avoid all spoilers in the thirteen year stretch. All I know is there's a pig called Colin or something. Anyway, I'm very excited to finally play it, as I've only ever heard good things about it.

Another game I'd like to experience for the first time is It Takes Two. My lady love and I are looking for our next co-op adventure after completing Split Fiction, so what better choice than Hazelight's other phenomenal game?

Oh, and if I get time, I'd also like to check out Routine. It isn't exactly giving warm and cosy vibes, but I'm worried it could leave Xbox Game Pass soon, and with GTA 6 on the horizon I don't have spare funds floating around.

I've got quite a lot going on this weekend, so I don't expect to be playing too much. Hopefully I might be able to fit in some more Star Wars Galactic Racer and Tape to Tape though - both of those games are so incredible!

Final Fantasy VII Remake Intergrade on Xbox Game Pass is also something I'm planning to spend a lot of time with, possibly when I go on holiday in a few weeks' time. I played the demo and loved it, so now it's time to try the full thing!

#4147. Marathon’s Symbiosis Update Adds Host Of New Modes, Including Permanent PvE, Next Month

Bungie has detailed its upcoming Symbiosis update for Marathon, which introduces several significant modes next month. Chief among them is the new permanent PvE mode, which Bungie previously experimented with and promised earlier this year.

Symbiosis is headlined by Expedition, a co-op PvE destination with roguelite elements. Expedition pits teams of players against escalating challenges and offers randomized upgrades called Flash Boosts to increase their odds of success.

The Perimeter zone has also been expanded with the new Burrows and Reservoir areas. Another addition is Limbo, a new social hub for players to gather that features a firing range. You can also try out the new sword-wielding Bishop Runner Shell alongside new weapons and gear, such as the Maverick pistol, throwing knife, hack grenade, and V17 flamethrower. Lastly, you can test your skills against other players in the beta PvP Deathmatch mode.

Symbiosis arrives in Marathon on December 8. An open play week will kick off the same day, allowing new players to experience all of Marathon’s content for free until December 15.

The Symbiosis update marks Marathon's evolution into a more co-op-friendly, PvE experience as its initial focus on PvP extraction has struggled to sustain a substantial audience since its March 5 launch. Bungie announced in September that it plans to spend the rest of 2026 improving Marathon's core mechanics and features while giving players more agency for how they engage with it beyond competitive PvP.

For more on Marathon, check out our review.

#4146. All the hype has already made Crimson Desert one of the biggest launches on Steam this year

We're merely days away from the end of the first quarter of 2026, and Crimson Desert has come in clutch to join the list of big sellers.

Crimson Desert, the open-world action RPG off-shoot from Korean MMO Black Desert Online, has officially launched, nearly six years after it was initially revealed. The game has been building up a lot of momentum over the years, which recently coalesced to turn it into one of 2026’s most anticipated titles.

All of it has been leading up to this moment, and the game appears to have landed smoothly, though not without controversy, as has seemingly become part of its MO.

It has not been 24 hours since Crimson Desert launched on PC and consoles, and it’s already become a big hit. On Steam, one of two stores where the game can be purchased (the other being the Epic Games Store), the game shot to the top of the charts.

The action RPG continued to accumulate more and more players on Steam, peaking at a very respectable 239,045 concurrent players (via SteamDB). Though its success was very much expected, we perhaps didn’t predict its peak would be that high.

Indeed, Crimson Desert has been in Steam’s top 100 global sellers list for six weeks, jumping up six spots to become the number one seller this week just before it launched. As we get closer to the weekend, the numbers could climb even higher.

This peak concurrent puts Crimson Desert in the same league as several of the other major releases of the first quarter of 2026. The top spot continues to belong to Slay the Spire 2, which peaked at a staggering 574,638 concurrent players. It happened just days after the juggernaut Resident Evil Requiem achieved its own 344,214 peak concurrent, which was the year’s highest up until Slay the Spire 2’s release. All three are well ahead of Nioh 3’s 88,045 peak concurrent, and Marathon’s nearly identical peak of 88,337.

Crimson Desert has seen something of a mixed reception by critics. James gave it three stars in our review, saying it “lacks the connective sinew to be truly functional,” which is a common criticism shared by other outlets. Many also lamented the sheer number of systems fighting for player attention, its poorly explained mechanics, and counterintuitive controls.

On Steam, at least, players have similarly been divided, with the current Steam user rating sitting at Mixed, based on 8,728 reviews. Unsurprisingly, most of the negative reactions fall on the clunky controls and the game’s tendency to, as one Steam user put it, “so miserably tries to be everything at once, and fails to be anything at all.”

If you’re just getting started in Crimson Desert yourself, or plan to do so soon, we recommend reading these crucial tips to help orient yourself in the game’s vast world. You should also plan your initial skill unlocks by prioritising these skills to spend your Abyss Artifacts first.

#4145. Crimson Desert's first patch aims at fixing controls, but it mostly affects mouse and keyboard

The first post-launch patch for Crimson Desert is here, and the list of changes is promising, even if it doesn't go far enough to address some deeper issues.

Crimson Desert has been out for a few days now, and as positive as its been received by many players, the game suffers from several fundamental issues that anyone who’s played it has called out.

Perhaps the loudest one of those has been how the game controls, which is a problem that stems from the complexity of controls themselves, as well as the underlying animations behind many of the actions the player character performs.

In the first case, at least, something is being done.

Developer Pearl Abyss rolled out patch 1.00.03 for Crimson Desert on Monday. The patch is available now on Steam and PlayStation, with Xbox and the Epic Games Store following “at a later time.”

Today’s update follows a letter to players the developer issued on Saturday. The letter generally acknowledged player feedback, but specifically pointed to complaints about the game’s clunky controls as something of a focus for the team.

The action RPG has actually broken its launch peak concurrent player numbers over the weekend, though only by a few thousands more. Its Steam user review rating has also improved over the same period.

This latest update only includes an initial set of fixes, but Pearl Abyss vowed to keep working on addressing all other points of feedback. A highlight in 1.00.03 is the addition of a Storage at Howling Hill Camp, which can be used to store inventory items.

The most important changes, of course, affect how the game controls on keyboard and mouse. Pearl Abyss included several fixes and altered some of the default presets to make the experience less painful when playing the game with a keyboard and mouse.

There are sadly no changes to controllers, but it is something that the developer said we can expect to see in future patches. More improvements for keyboard and mouse setups are in the works, too.

Beyond the control changes, patch 1.00.03 also includes a set of gameplay tweaks, especially when it comes to enemy health and difficulty. It also makes fast travelling more convenient, and brings a few fixes to NPC dialogue. You can read the full change log on Steam.

If you’re deep in Crimson Desert already, we definitely recommend giving our guides a look. We recently added new pages to help you figure out where to socket your Abyss Gear, how to find Contribution Points - and where to spend them, as well as more generally helpful information like how to expand your inventory, and how to reveal the map.

#4144. Surprising Literally Nobody, Grand Theft Auto VI Is The Most Pre-Ordered Game In PlayStation And Xbox Store History

Grand Theft Auto VI launches next week on Thursday, November 19. You can preload the game on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S starting today, as detailed by Rockstar Games, PlayStation, and Xbox. Alongside this announcement, both PlayStation and Xbox have revealed that – surprise! – GTA VI is the most preordered game in the history of their respective digital stores.

That's not shocking – GTA VI is, by many metrics, the most anticipated game in history, with its predecessor, Grand Theft Auto V, selling nearly 235 million copies since its launch back in 2013. There's also the fact that Rockstar Games is not releasing a physical edition of GTA VI, per se. Yes, you can go to a store to pick up a GTA VI box (and you can do so today, allowing you to preload the game), but inside that box will be a download code for a digital version of the game – you won't find GTA VI on a physical disc. So, naturally, many players are opting to purchase the game on digital storefronts like the PlayStation and Xbox game stores.

"Grand Theft Auto VI, the most preordered title of all time on the Microsoft Store, launches November 19," an Xbox blog post reads. "Considering the unprecedented demand, we encourage everyone to begin preloading as soon as possible to ensure you're prepared for launch day." PlayStation echoes this statement with a blog post of its own that reads, "Grand Theft Auto VI is now the most preordered game in the history of the PlayStation Store. Given this unprecedented demand, we've joined with Rockstar Games to allow players to start preloading the game nine days early, so they're ready to play on launch day."

There you have it: People are very excited about Grand Theft Auto VI.

Grand Theft Auto VI launches next week on November 19 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S.

For more, check out the song "Pusher" from the game's original score, then check out the GTA VI launch trailer. After that, check out this exclusive story about how GTA VI features over 170 animal species and another about its tropical storms and hurricanes. Be sure to read about how GTA VI will target 30 FPS gameplay on all consoles, too.

#4143. Rumour: Samsung's New Chip Process Kicks Off 'Nintendo Switch 2 Lite' Speculation

Update: Digital Foundry weighs in on the rumour

Update [Mon 9th Nov 2026, 4:45pm]: At the end of last month, we covered a rumour that Nintendo was working on a 'Switch 2 Lite' model that would supposedly utilise a new chip process in the works at Samsung.

We clarified at the time that it was all nothing more than a rumour, and now the tech experts over at Digital Foundry have popped up to add their ten cents' worth to the conversation. Unsurprisingly, they don't have a whole lot of faith in the idea.

The biggest reason for the outlet's dismissal is the lack of any solid sourcing that Nintendo is looking to downsize its hardware in the first place. "The existence of Samsung materials for a new process that could be used for a handheld doesn't say much on its own," DF says, claiming that the rumoured specs look "more like guesswork".

Then there's the technical side of things, with DF noting that Switch 2 already uses a bespoke processor, so it's not like the transition to the new 8LPU+ would come easily. On top of that, it deems the chip process' rumoured 15% drop in power consumption as "nice to have, but doesn't yield the transformative battery improvements required for a smaller revision" — the original jump from Switch to Switch Lite roughly halved power consumption, let's not forget.

Still, the rumour remains exactly that, a rumour, for the time being. Samsung should spill the beans on the new process next month, but until then, it might be best to continue taking everything with a pinch of salt.

News Is Switch 2 Lite Possible, Thanks to New Samsung Chip Technology?

Digital FoundrySpecs have appeared online, but something doesn't make sense.

Original Story: Samsung reportedly has a new chip in the works that could help make dreams of a 'Switch 2 Lite' a reality (thanks for the heads up, Notebook Check).

As shared on Bluesky by Nintendo Patents Watch, Samsung has supposedly been working on a new 8LPU+ chip process which might be able to assist with making the Nvidia chip inside Switch 2 more compact and more powerful, while drawing on less power.

While the chip itself hasn't been officially revealed yet (South Korean outlet Electronic Times reports that it could be unveiled in December), the word on the street is that the chip process will boast a 12% performance enhancement, 15% power reduction, and an 8% area shrink, among other features, making it a prime candidate for, we don't know, a smaller console.

At the IEDM 2026, Samsung is scheduled to present its 2nd-gen 8nm process 8LPU+: • 12% performance enhancement • 15% power reduction • 8% area shrink • ~10% I/O area reduction • Stand-by leakage reduction Is this Nvidia and Nintendo’s plan all along for the Switch 2 Lite? 1/

With Samsung behind the custom Nvidia chip already in the Switch 2, there's every chance that the new tech could also be used in Nintendo's favour. A smaller Switch 2 — perhaps borrowing the portable-first, non-dock USPs of its predecessor's Lite model — might even pose a cheaper alternative for those wanting to get in on the new hardware's exclusives. With rising costs on just about everything (particularly in the tech space), a less powerful Switch 2 model with cheaper components sure does sound appealing.

We've also got to remember that Nintendo is wrapping up Switch 1 distribution in February 2027. It doesn't necessarily mean that something will be coming in to replace it, we should point out, but if Nintendo and Samsung do have something in the works, it'd be a prime time to introduce it. Heck, the original Switch Lite was released a mere two and a half years after the base model, so who's to say Nintendo doesn't have a Switch 2 equivalent in store for late 2028?

Of course, we've already seen the smallest Switch 2 revision already this year, with the replaceable battery model being introduced in Europe. Rumblings of an 'OLED model' remain under the surface as ever, but what if a 'Lite' option pops up first? Only time will tell, eh!

I played the original Football Manger games when they first came out on a very basic PC (as they were back then), and played them for hours upon hours. I absolutely loved them. Something tells me I might have had the game on my ZX Spectrum too in the early 80s, but that might be my memory playing havoc with me as it often does these days, though in fairness, I am thinking back to over 40 years ago!

Anyway, seeing Football Manager 27 coming to Game Pass in the next few days does give me the urge to give it ago to see if I can rekindle some old and fond memories. It would also then be the very first game I have played on Game Pass this year, which would be a bonus...!

Let's see...40 years ago, I bought my first computer - a Commodore 128. It was most useful for the Go64 command, which put it in C64 mode, to run all those games. My favorite was the original Loderunner. My first video game system was the original VCS though, much earlier. I can actually remember visiting friends' houses and playing their Pong systems, which if memory serves correctly (like your memory FB - not so well) was a Magnavox system. My favorite computer was the Amiga, purchased back in around 1987...and 1988, and later but I don't remember when. I owned the 1000, 500, 2000 and 3000 systems at one time or another. My fondest, early, video game event was turning over 1M points in Asteroids (VCS), and quitting about 500K points later, because I was getting tired and bored. Anyway, what was your earliest memories @Fiendish-Beaver ?

My earliest memory of gaming is the first time I ever encountered it, @Droopy. My Father died when I was 6 weeks old in January of 1964, and my Mother raised me alone. However, as my Mother worked, each Summer holiday, I would be dispatched to my Aunts and Uncles who lived about 200 miles North of where I lived, and I would spend 6 weeks in the company of my Cousins.

In the Summer of 1973, at the age of 10, I went to my Cousins as was customary, to find that they had a games machine that played Pong (to my recollection, that is all it played although that might be the only game they had) and I played the game as much as my Cousins would tolerate for the entire 6 weeks. Obviously, they were far better at it than me, but that did not stop hours and hours of fun. It's probably difficult to imagine now, but think what it must have been like to go from never having heard of gaming, to encountering it for the first time. It was mind blowing to 10 year old me! By the end of the holiday, I was absolutely hooked.

The first console that I owned myself was an Intellivision console that I bought in 1982 with money that I earned working for British Sugar stacking huge sacks of er, well... sugar! The sacks weighed almost as much as I did, which as I weighed less than 10 stone at the time probably isn't that much, but the work paid really well. Whilst I do not remember how many games I had for it, one does stick out, and that was Tron Deadly Discs. It was very basic, but you simply had to throw discs to destroy the robots within an arena, and you could enter doors that would sort of teleport you around the arena. I always remember the game because of one night where I just didn't seem capable of dying, and because you could not save the game (and I'm not sure you could pause it either) I just kept playing until something like 4 a.m. even though I had to be up at 6 to go to work! That night I got my highest ever score in the game, and also formed probably one of my fondest memories in gaming too. It just felt epic! I imagine these days, faced with the same game, I'd be bored inside an hour, but back then, it felt like the hight of entertainment.

Effectively, I have been gaming for about 53 years now, and owned at least one console since the age of 18. I've owned an Intellivision console, a Sinclair ZX Spectrum, various Amstrad computers, various Commodore consoles, various Nintendo's, various Sega's, each of the PlayStation and Xbox consoles, and a gaming PC.

I injured my back in 1990/1, and it became increasingly bad as time progressed to the point that I had to medically retire from the Police in 2010. Fortunately, my time in Bomb Disposal and the Police meant that I was able to retire with a reasonable pension, and whilst I have not been able to work for the past 16 years, I have been able to game every day since, so injuring my back has had it's upsides even if I cannot walk particularly well or far! So, every cloud and what have you... 😉

Thanks for posting @Fiendish-Beaver ! I always enjoy reading your posts, whether here or on Push Square's comments sections. I think I actually read more of Pure XBox's comments sections than I do Push Square's, so I miss some Push Square comments' posts. Frankly, I enjoy the users more here, although there is some caustic ones here as well...and some familiar ones as well! Anyway, yeah my mom bought me my first Atari VCS, better known as the Atari 2600...as far as I remember, one of the more loving things she did for me. She felt sorry for me missing out. I couldn't always borrow my older brother's unit. What a cool thing to have happen to a child! She's no longer with us, but I still love her for it. I suppose parents buying their child a video game system is common now, what with all the pricing(!). But it was really special back then...especially for me. I can't remember the year - had to be 197x when it happened. Not sure! Kudos to all parents for buying their kids video game systems. In the language of the 70's, that is really cool! I got a loving wife now, that lets me buy whatever floats in my imagination. That's really cool too! You don't find something like that...well, at all in a lot of people's cases. But, I found one! Of course, I married her because she had a good heart. What profound wisdom was I reading at the time? It's worth more than gold to me! You can't buy people that really love you. And we play couch coop nearly every week. Borderlands 4, Serious Sam, Gears (All of them!). I've got the latest Gears (forget what it's called, oh yeah Eday (Emergence Day)), we haven't bothered to even play it yet! LOL We'll love it when we do - we finished all the others, several times, and loved them. Where can you get a wife that is happy when you're happy, and loves video games? Ah well, some thing's are priceless. Remember that men! (and some women!) Wow - I forgot what we were talking about. Oh the old times! Yeah, great stories for sure. Keep them coming...I enjoy reading them! We are lucky we live in the now though, know what I mean? Look at all we can play now! Think of all we've been through, and played through - the birth of video games! A lot of people aren't with us any longer that enjoyed video and computer games. We're the lucky ones! We made it! (We're still gaming!) Sorry, it's Sunday and someone's gotta preach...

#4141. Australia Did It: End-of-the-World Railway Defense Business Review - Delivering Where It Matters

Australia Did It: End-of-the-world Railway Defense Business is a game I catch myself playing in my head long after I shut it off. Though it uses turn-based strategy as its base, it expands beyond the genre’s regular confines, blending elements from roguelikes, puzzle games, bullet-heaven titles, and the tower-defense genre. The result is an experience that demands wide-scale experimentation and rewards improvisation.

In a post-apocalyptic world where the Atlantic Ocean has dried up, you risk your life to ensure your shipment reaches its destination. Riding from station to station by train, you must build your team amid your many missions as various mutated creatures, malicious machines, and coordinated soldiers attack your convoy. Lore is doled out piecemeal and serves mostly as background dressing, but each time I learned more about the world, I became more curious.

To survive the harshness of the wasteland, you must use cindermint, an in-game resource gained for surviving turns and killing enemies, to spawn defenders, with three base classes to choose from. The revolver-wielding Gunslinger is your primary damage dealer, while the Radshot applies corrosive radiation damage, and the Nomad offers a close-range shotgun blast with knockback.

Those base-level characters offer solid variety upon which to build. And that’s where the main hook for Australia Did It comes in: experimentation through combination. In the midst of battle, you can merge two units of the same level to create new, more powerful defenders, influenced by the traits of those used in the merge. At the onset, you can merge two Nomads to create a level 2 Nomad with increased damage and knockback, but the real fun comes in combining disparate units to create completely new characters. Even now, more than 15 hours into my gameplay, I’m still concocting new combinations I want to try on my next run.

By the end of my first successful run, I had multiple level 6 characters, including a railgun-toting heavy, mages who steal health from enemies and redistribute it to nearby allies, a drone that can move beyond the walls of the station to attack enemies directly, and, my personal favorite, a dual-shotgun-wielding one-man wrecking crew. However, many of these higher-level units also possess drawbacks to consider, like the railgun scorching all adjacent tiles or the drone running out of battery if it’s outside the walls for too long. Though I started keeping notes in my head about which combinations led to my favorite results, I was grateful for a comprehensive compendium that tracked the tens of unit types I unlocked through this rewarding experimentation.

The meat of the experience places your squad on a 25-tile square board with enemies spawning from the four principal directions. Thoughtfulness and positioning are crucial, as each unit on your squad possesses different traits and movement efficiency, as do the encroaching enemies. Basic enemies often make a beeline toward the station, while others may take a weaving route or keep their distance and blast you at range. Improvising and adjusting your strategy on the fly is the most engaging part of Australia Did It, and when you perfectly adapt in the moment, or escape the scenario by the skin of your teeth, there are few better feelings I’ve experienced in a game this year.

Your goal in this phase is to simply defend the station and gather resources to strengthen your squad before evacuating and moving on to the next area. Considering each unit's strengths, weaknesses, and capabilities while strategically positioning them around the station takes some getting used to, especially during the more chaotic stages. I fist-pumped as I watched the train pull out of a station that was about to crumble, and I lamented the loss of high-level units I had to leave behind to ensure the survival of the convoy. The process is ceaselessly thrilling, even as you begin to see how the gears work under the hood. I just wish I could say the same about the intervening train sections.

Once you escape the turn-based strategy portion, your surviving squad members hop aboard the train and chart their route. Using a basic map, you choose your next stop, with factors like enemy types and modifiers shown to you ahead of time. The top-down train segments between station-defense stages are largely passive; the units you evacuated from the previous station automatically attack swarming enemies with the same traits and perks they have in the main gameplay areas. You can aim a focus cone to instruct your units, but you’re at the mercy of the units you’ve brought. You can trigger an ultimate ability to send your defenders into overdrive, but I rarely needed it.

While I love the idea of intentionally crafting a team that’s good at both the turn-based strategy and bullet-heaven transport sections, I was never fully engaged getting from point A to point B. Instead, I often caught myself checking how much longer before my train arrived at the next station; these sections can be completed in a minute or two, but that doesn’t alleviate the feeling that it’s a step down from the other gameplay. These novel portions aren’t bad by any means; they’re merely an average part of an otherwise excellent experience.

Looking back on the hours I poured into Australia Did It, the forgettable train segments will occupy only a small part of my memories, just as they do in each run. Instead, what will stick with me for months to come are the creative combination mechanics, the outstanding turn-based defense system, and the thrill of uncovering the mysteries of this bleak, yet engaging world.

DC is reportedly rebooting for the second time in three years

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

It looks like it's out with the old and in with the new at DC, as Skydance (the name of the newly merged Paramount and Warner Bros.) is reportedly set to scrap the James Gunn and Peter Safran-built DCU.

News broke yesterday that Gunn and Safran were out as co-CEOs of DC Studios, and as Hollywood digests the fallout, new details are emerging.

According to reliable former The Hollywood Reporter journalist Matt Belloni's What I'm Hearing newsletter, the DCU as we know it might be over. He writes: "I'm told plans are already afoot to dismantle much of what Gunn and Safran had plotted out beyond next summer's Gunn-directed Man of Tomorrow, the currently shooting The Batman: Part 2, and an in-the-works HBO series. So DC goes back into reboot mode… again."

A separate report from The Hollywood Reporter says Gunn was working on a script for a third Superman film, with a plan for a new Superman movie every two years, potentially leading to the Justice League.

"There have been so many highs along the way: releasing Superman and Clayface, making Peacemaker, reading the scripts to The People Vs., the entire process of Man of Tomorrow, which thus far has been the best filmmaking experience of my life, and numerous other moments," Gunn shared on his Instagram in a lengthy statement about his time as co-CEO of DC Studios.

Elsewhere in the statement, he wrote: "So, yes, I will miss the people around me, and I will miss being the co-caretaker of these great characters, but I'm also incredibly relieved and excited to get back to pure filmmaking. That's not to say Peter and I are immediately done with DC or superheroes. We have Man of Tomorrow out this summer. And we've just been engaged on another DC project which I'm writing, and we'll see where it goes after that. And of course, the characters we set up will live on."

At the moment, it's not clear what, if any, of the DCU Chapter One: Gods and Monsters slate will get made after Man of Tomorrow. We'll just have to wait and see.

Next up for DC is Man of Tomorrow, which arrives on July 9, 2027. You can keep track of what's coming this year with our guide to all the upcoming movies worth getting excited about.

#4139. Stalker 2’s first expansion officially revealed, and it's taking us to the power plant where it all began

Stalker 2’s first add-on isn’t far off, and it may just be the thing to bring you back to post-apocalyptic Chornobyl in 2026.

One of the biggest reveals out of today’s Xbox Partner Preview showcase has been the new Stalker 2 expansion. The developer did tease some sort of announcement ahead of the event, but I don’t think an expansion was on many of our bingo cards.

Cost of Hope is the big news; a new add-on that the developer has wisely decided to reveal fairly close to release. Or, at least, the planned release target.

First off, Cost of Hope is set for release this summer. It’ll arrive on all current platforms simultaneously, meaning PC, Xbox, and PlayStation. The expansion is described as “non-linear”, and it takes place in the heartlands, deeper into the Zone.

The story revolves around a conflict between Duty, and Freedom, two factions whose idea of the what the Zone is and their understanding of its possibilities differ widely. You’ll be playing as protagonist Skif once again, and the expansion’s events will run parallel to the main game.

GSC Game World says Cost of Hope will introduce two new regions, offering dozens of hours of gameplay. We’ll get to actually explore the Chornobyl Nuclear Power Plant as part of the expansion, alongside the Iron Forest.

Each of the two new regions will have its own hub area, NPCs, quests, activities and stories. Of course, it wouldn’t be a Stalker expansion without some new weapons, and Cost of Hope promises a few - some can even be seen in the trailer.

The developer also confirmed that there’s one other story DLC in the works. Together with Heart of Chornobyl, and Cost of Hope all three will form a trilogy of interconnected stories. More details on Cost of Hope - including a release date - will be revealed sometime in the summer.

#4138. Bandai Namco Shuts Down Unknown 9: Awakening Developer Reflector Entertainment

Bandai Namco has announced it is shutting down Reflector Entertainment, the Montreal studio behind 2024’s Unknown 9: Awakening.

Reflector, founded in 2015, is a subsidiary of Bandai Namco that was acquired in 2020. Unknown 9: Awakening is the studio’s only released title, which was first revealed at Gamescom 2020 and released on October 17, 2024. The third-person action game is set within the broader Unknown 9 transmedia franchise, which includes a book trilogy, comics, and a web series, and stars Haroona, a woman able to traverse a separate dimension called the Fold. Haroona, played by The Witcher actress Anya Chalotra, uses this ability and other supernatural powers to battle a hostile secret society across India and other global locations.

Upon release, Unknown 9: Awakening didn’t make much of a critical splash; it currently has a 59 Metascore and "Mixed" Steam reviews. In November 2024, a month after Unknown 9's launch, Reflector laid off 18 percent of its staff.  More layoffs were announced in January 2025 as Reflector canned an unannounced project while confirming Unknown 9 failed to meet expectations. With Reflector’s dissolution, Bandai Namco expects to post “an extraordinary loss” of approximately €21 million on its Q3 financial results for the fiscal year ending March 31, 2027.

#4136. Never one to lag behind HSR and ZZZ, Genshin Impact will introduce its own new pink-haired animal-themed girl in Version Luna 6

Plus Mondstadt is expanding yet further north in Genshin Impact's Luna 6 update.

Today’s Genshin Impact Special Program has wrapped up, and it’s brought us some big news about the next major update. Luna 6 is the next phase in the action RPG’s story, titled Song of the Welkin Moon: Rondo - Augured Homecoming.

It’s set to arrive on April 8, bringing with it a tonne of new content, including a big expansion to the original region of Mondstadt.

As part of this new update, Mondstadt’s northern parts expand with new areas. The new Dornman Port is one thing, but the most exciting is the Temple of Space. This floating structure is home to Asmoday fragments, and is made up of different realms inspired by Liyue, Sumeru, and various other civilizations from around Teyvat. Launching with the update is a new mechanic that lets you manipulate the space to reveal hidden paths containing secrets.

If you take the time to explore, you’ll find a lot to there to learn about Asmoday, Ruler of Space. There’s a new boss to take on in the temple, too: Watcher: Fallen Vigil.

The only new character in Luna 6 is Linnea, who continues the current trend within HoYoverse games of focussing heavily on cute pink-haired animal-themed girls. Linnea is a 5-Star Geo Bow user who can really work with parties made up of Lunar-Crystallize characters, with her big gimmick being the ability to turn Hydro-Crystallize reactions into Lunar-Crystallize reactions.

Linnea has a companion, Lumi, who allows her to increase the Lunar-Crystallize damage she deals, while also lowering her enemies’ Geo resistance. Linnea can also deliver either off-field Geo damage or a Lunar-Crystallize reaction hit with her Elemental Skill.

Beyond that, she can heal the party using her Elemental Burst. If you take Linnea with you as you explore, she can help you discover rare animals, thanks to her innate naturalist abilities.

This update will also see Chasca get her first-ever rerun, and you’ll be able to roll for her in the first phase of Event Wishes. The second phase will feature no new characters and instead focus on Nefer and Lauma. There’s going to be another Chronicled Wish banner, this time specifically for Fontaine characters.

You can look forward to a few other new arrivals in Luna 6, including The Nod-Krai Trade Expo, some quality of life updates to Miliastra Wonderland to up the number of players in each lobby, not to mention various other UI changes.

#4135. Poll: Which Zelda: Ocarina Of Time HUD Option Is Your Favourite?

Just like the open-world entries that precede it, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on Switch 2 comes with a handful of HUD options, so you can play with as much or as little on-screen information as you please.

In our first few hours with the game, we played around with all three of these options, getting to grips with the pros and cons of all of them. Most of us settled on one after a little while, and now we're keen to see where you lovely lot have ended up.

As a reminder, there are three different HUD options in the settings menu's 'In-Game Interface Tab': Normal, Pro, and Master. The first of these is listed as your "Standard display," with your mini map, item selection, D-pad options, life/magic meters, and button prompts all appearing on the screen. It offers the most information you can get at a glance, but it can look a little cluttered for some.

The 'Pro' option tones things down a little, displaying "minimal information," according to its settings definition. This one does away with almost all the info we mentioned above, but button prompts (for 'Talk' or 'Grab' selections) and Navi's speech bubbles still make an appearance. This is a ripe choice for anyone who knows their Zelda mechanics, but still wants to know when something is there to be interacted with.

'Master' mode is the most stripped back of the bunch, offering a "display with no information". This means that everything other than the main gameplay is removed from the screen, and no prompts crop up as you approach NPCs or interactive items. And yes, that includes your targeting cursor. This option keeps things stripped back to the bare minimum and arguably provides the most immersive experience of the bunch, but there's every chance that you'll miss the odd detail (or Navi quip) along the way.

Each setting has its perks, to be sure, and we're not about to say that any one of them is the 'correct' way to play, but still, we're interested to know what mode you have been rocking with so far.

You can let us know your preferred HUD option in the following poll, then take to the comments to let us know why it's stuck.

Which option have you been maining? Let us know in the comments.

#4134. PlayStation Cancels In-Development Live-Service Shooter, Fairgames, At Jade Raymond's Former Haven Studio

PlayStation has reportedly canceled Fairgames, the long-in-development live-service shooter being made by Haven Studios, which Jade Raymond founded in 2021. Sony acquired Haven in 2022, and in 2025, Raymond left the studio, though it remained dedicated to developing Fairgames without her. It seems the story of Fairgames is now over, according to a new Bloomberg report.

The publication reports that PlayStation will not enforce any job cuts or layoffs as a result of Fairgames' cancellation, which comes as a surprise, and the studio will instead shift to support other first-party teams under the PlayStation umbrella. According to Bloomberg, this cancellation comes after a recent test of the game that allowed "thousands of players" to check it out did not deliver the results PlayStation wanted.

"While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set," PlayStation executives Sean Decker and John Doyle wrote in an email to employees today, according to Bloomberg. "Combined with challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game."

This doesn't necessarily come as a surprise. PlayStation announced Fairgames back in 2023 and hasn't shown much since, leaving many to assume development has been struggling behind the scenes. Since then, PlayStation has pulled back heavily on its live-service plans, which originally included launching more than 10 live-service games by March of this year. Naughty Dog's Last of Us multiplayer game was canceled, Bungie ended active development on Destiny 2, and live-service Horizon spin-off Hunters Gathering is reportedly being overhauled following poor playtest feedback, amongst other stories. Reading between the lines, many fans were waiting for news like today's cancellation of Fairgames to drop.

Still, in an era where games are canceled and entire teams are laid off (sometimes even after releasing a successful game), it's nice to see Haven employees are not facing layoffs.

#4133. Caleb's third Myth has finally arrived in Love and Deepspace, and it's good news for all the husbandbro fans out there

Love and Deepspace has kicked off a new event, squarely built around Caleb's new Memory Pair.

Love and Deepspace’s latest update is here, adding a new Memory Pair for Caleb. The event is dubbed Ghosts' Final March, and it’s available now as part of a new Limited Wish Pool, as it has always worked.

The new Memory Pair is a 5-Star Solar-Slot, which can be obtained through the aforementioned Wish Pool. Doing so will unlock the Netherlord Companion for Caleb, and there’s even more for you to explore in this one.

Alongside the big new Memory Pair, Ghosts' Final March also offers the opportunity to earn a new 4-Star Solar-Slot Memory Pair, alongside ten Deepspace Wishes, 500 Diamonds, and other freebies. The event ends on April 11, so you have some time to get in and play.

If you’re only interested in the 5-Star variants, you’ll be happy to know that Infold is sticking with 150 pulls as the absolute maximum to guarantee earning Netherlord. This will be automatically unlocked after you pull both Nether Yearning and Nether Parting through the Wish Pool.

Obtaining either of the two will give you access to all chapters for the new Myth that’s also available as part of this event: Yin Yang Sundering. You can read all the lore once either of the two Memories have been unlocked, and you won’t even need to upgrade either of them.

The Lost Souls event has also kicked off alongside the new update. You can take part to claim a 4-Star Solar Slor Memory Pair for Caleb: Duskshard Dreams and Duskshard Lotus. You can also earn the 3-Star Memory, Lotus Bond, alongside some other freebies like more Wishes, Diamonds, Photo Poses, and an event-exclusive title.

After you unlock Caleb’s Netherlord Companion, you may want to fight alongside him to get another 4-Star Memory for free. You’ll need to challenge the the Rehearsal Stage to do so, and your first clear is guaranteed to get you the Duskshard Lotus Memory.

If you’re new to Love and Deepspace, or you simply want a refresher, we’ve put together a guide to help you wrap your head around Myths; how they work and how to unlock them. Banners are also an important part of any gacha game, Love and Deepspace included, so here’s how banners work, and what the current and next banners are.

#4132. Talking Point: What Made The Xbox 360 Era So Incredible In Your Opinion?

As we continue celebrating the past 25 years of Xbox throughout the course of the month, we thought we'd use this opportunity to look at the Xbox 360 - a console that's consistently rated as the best system in the history of the brand.

The Xbox 360 will be turning 21 years old on November 22nd, and its impact is still being felt today. This is the console that gave us such features as Party Chat, modern-style Xbox dashboards, the ability to download mainstream games digitally, and a ridiculous number of incredible franchises that have won over the hearts and minds of many.

For what it's worth, we did actually talk about some of this stuff for the 20th anniversary last year:

Feature Seven Things We Miss About The Xbox 360 Era In 2025

As we rapidly approach its 20th anniversary

With that said though, every era of Xbox has treated us to innovative new features and amazing games that have stood the test of time. The PS3 existed at the same time as the Xbox 360, and yet somehow, Microsoft's console felt like the more popular of the two, despite selling slightly less units overall in the end.

It even managed to navigate a devastating technical issue in the form of the Red Ring of Death, and somehow still convince the masses that it was one of the greatest consoles of all time. That's some feat.

So, what made the Xbox 360 era so incredible in your opinion? Was it just a brilliantly-designed system, RROD aside? Did it innovate in ways that no other system did? Were the games simply that good? Or has its popularity become overblown since the horribly botched launch of the Xbox One in 2013?

Let us know your thoughts on why the Xbox 360 era was so good down in the comments section below.

Exclusive Xbox 360 Fan Talks To Us About Completing Their Collection After 20 Years

"My mission is to get achievements in every single game..."

Fraser is the News Editor at Pure Xbox, where he spends his time reporting on the biggest stories in the world of Xbox and beyond.

It had all the best titles, plenty of exclusives and the broadest content. It was an exciting platform

What made it special was creative games, exclusives and visual gap: innovative titles for their time, featuring beautiful HD 3D graphics and smooth gameplay. It was also the era of creative games and iconic franchises like Gears of War, Mass Effect, Dead Space, and BioShock.

I feel like this is the formula that Asha is trying to recreate with Helix: a return to exclusive games and a revolutionary technical platform. What's still missing is the creativity aspect, and that's where I still have some doubts, just as I do about the industry as a whole. Risk-taking has become minimal, and we're being flooded with remasters and sequels.

That said, considering the enormous cost of game development today, I can understand why risks have to be carefully calculated. Even so, Xbox has been by far the most creative platform of this console generation compared to its competitors, so hopefully that continues.

The Xbox 360 featured an exclusive title called Lost Odyssey, arguably the greatest JRPG ever created. While most JRPGs are aimed at a younger audience and tend to feature straightforward, simple narratives, Lost Odyssey takes a different approach. Its core, titled "A Thousand Years of Dreams, A Thousand Years of Memories"—which explores the protagonist’s past—was penned by Kiyoshi Shigematsu, a recipient of the prestigious Naoki Prize. These stories delve into universal themes: the experience of loss and separation, a profound sense of emptiness, and the sorrow of having neither a place to return to nor a destination to head toward. Much of this content is written with those in the twilight of their lives in mind.The main storyline is also rooted in the personal tragedies experienced by the project’s executive producer, Hironobu Sakaguchi.The game boasts a top-tier creative team, including character designs by Takehiko Inoue (Slam Dunk, Vagabond) and a musical score by Nobuo Uematsu—some of the finest talent to ever work on an Xbox title.Even today, many fans continue to hope for a remake or a sequel.

It was the same as what made movies in the 80's to early 90's great- even if they were bad, usually there was fun to be had. Publishers and developers were less afraid of taking risks and even less afraid of offending some perpetually-agitated malcontent who would never buy their products in the first place. They also heavily invested almost 2 decades and lots of money to shoehorn in "creators" who hate the media and its consumers.

There also wasn't a corrupt cartel of militant, quid pro quo grifters posing as self-appointed moral authorities nobody ever asked for destroying the content as part of a contemporary campaign against the '4 Olds', and working in Lockstep with the world's largest equity firms trying to curate our culture for their financial gain and societal control.

Back then, Xbox was focused on providing pure entertainment and making games that people genuinely enjoyed. During the Xbox One generation, it tried to shift its focus toward TV and health-related initiatives, but that ultimately failed. In the Xbox Series X|S generation, the focus seems to have moved more toward politics, and there have been very few truly gamer-focused AAA titles. That's why I love the Xbox 360 era.

I have been a fan of Xbox since day 1, make no mistake. And in those polls, I typically vote for the original Xbox.

But Xbox 360 is objectively the only successful Xbox console. I make arguments for the original, as it was breaking into an impossible market, and in that aspect, it was successful. But there's no arguing against 360. It could not be ignored. It dominated the zeitgeist.

Lets not forget that IGN's presentations on Xbox LIVE was truly breath taking and constantly engaging. My PS3 seemed very dull and dead (to me) after I enjoyed, all those shows, reviews, trailers analysis, live gaming sessions with developers on Xbox 360. So, back then, just as I told to all my friends "Xbox 360 is a living console... So much happening in that... It is like, gaming universe all by itself... Electrifying... So, much fun"

Xbox 360's GPU was significantly stronger than PS3 GPU and was paying off significantly. I had to buy Dark Souls second time for Xbox 360 after I platiniumed it on PS3. So, I platiniumed it once more on Xbox 360 with even more joy, because graphics were (and still is) remarkably better. Dark Souls was not an exception because many other games had better graphics on Xbox 360 due to the stronger GPU.

We were younger and had more time to game.

The 360 was my first time with xbox and I particularly loved the live arcade. Geometry Wars and Trails HD are probably my most played games still today 😂 Well, except for Sensible World of Soccer on the Amiga.

My friend had a 360 and I had a PS3 at that time and we would often visit and play the other persons games to get an idea of what was on each device. Personally I think that what made that generation great was that it was a sweet spot for the cost and quality of games whilst still having a relatively short development timescale so there was always something new to play.

Also in the UK it was still the great time of Blockbuster game rentals. We rarely rented games but we would always go in and browse the ex-rentals because they would be sold off very cheap and you could get big titles for bargain prices.

To me, it just felt fresh and had a great library. One of the great consoles.

For me, it was the balance of GPU, CPU, and RAM that saw 360 versions of multiplats usually perform better than PS3 versions despite having weaker hardware as well as the indie games. Zombie Strippers Stole My Heart Then Ate My Brains is a bizarre mid-2000s gem that could only have existed (on console) on 360.

The Cave native ports for 360 are better than shot triggers in terms of performance. (Shot Triggers Series X if it happened I think could match it maybe?)

It still had traditional console games good Japanese support (Can understand why the commercial side disappointed though.)

It had the advantage of being the lead platform for many games. (This is what I don’t understand about many indie games where the majority of sales are on Switch why devs don’t at least give it a version suited for it if not make it the lead platform. The Steam sales are not going to go down significantly if it’s a good game. There is plenty of things that can just be toggled on. What I don’t understand is why when there a basically no ps or Xbox sales for these games. I get them on Xbox but I just don’t get it.) I do get optimising Unreal needs a AAA team. But if that is not possible using it and designing for Nintendo it’s not going to be bad elsewhere.

#4131. The Petit Planet beta is coming back with new updates, but you still need to hope for an invite

If you've been missing Petit Planet since it was last available to play, you'll be happy to know that HoYoverse is hosting another test soon.

It’s been quite a while since we’ve heard anything about Petit Planet, the upcoming game from Genshin Impact and Honkai: Star Rail developer HoYoverse. By most accounts, Petit Planet is the studio’s take on Animal Crossing, though with a few interesting ideas of its own.

The game’s most recent test took place all the way back in November, but its next big test isn’t far off.

HoYoverse announced today that Petit Planet’s Stardrift Test is scheduled for April 21. This latest build will be available on PC, Android, and iOS. The beta will include new Neighbors, an updated Starsea Voyage, and more for you to do at the Galactic Bazaar.

Seeing as interacting with Neighbors is a core part of this life sim RPG, the confirmation that new faces will be available in this test is big news. Each Neighbor in Petit Planet is a character, with their own personalty and life story.

The Starsea Voyage now includes a map, too, which you can use to take you to other Islets. If you played any of the previous tests, you should already be familiar with this feature.

The only bit of bad news here is that this remains a closed beta. You’re still encouraged to sign up on the official website, but you’re not guaranteed access. HoYoverse said that only a portion of players who sign up will be invited to the upcoming beta.

Petit Planet remains without a release date. If nothing else, it’ll be interesting to see the progress the game has made since last November’s beta.

#4130. Nintendo Switch 2 System Update 23.5.0 Is Now Live, Here Are The Full Patch Notes

Adds eShop gifting feature support and more

Nintendo has released a new firmware update for the Switch 2 this week, bumping it up to Version 23.5.0.

Most notably, it's added support for "gifting" eShop products to a Nintendo Account family group member. This is an "upcoming feature" and is scheduled to go live on 17th November 2026.

Apart from this, there's now also the ability to configure accessibility settings during the first-time setup, and there are some language updates. A Switch 1 update is out today as well, adding gifting feature support, and some general adjustments & fixes.

Here are the full patch notes for Version 23.5.0, courtesy of Nintendo's official support page:

Nintendo goes into some more detail about the gifting feature on its website, explaining how it can be used to give a child or family member a game for a special occasion.

You can send a gift by selecting the "Give as a Gift" option on an eShop product page, and even choose your gift wrap colour. From there, all the recipient has to do is accept the gift, and they can then play it.

The Version 23.5.0 update has also supposedly patched the recently discovered jailbreak exploit. You can find out more about this in our previous story. This latest update also follows a major Switch 2 system update (Version 23.0.0) in September, which added VRR for TV mode and much more.

Software "is not necessarily favorable either." In case you were wondering

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Nintendo president Shuntaro Furukawa says the house of Mario wants to keep the Switch 2 price as is despite surging hardware component prices. That said, there's only so long that can continue before a change of heart is considered.

Speaking to investors following an earnings report, the suits at Nintendo take a question regarding their thoughts on hardware and software pricing. Everything is getting more expensive, so at what point does Nintendo factor price increases into their planning?

When it comes to hardware, Furukawa says that Nintendo's reliance on various partners for different parts creates a greater sense of vulnerability when things beyond its control go wrong.

"Currently, manufacturing costs are trending upward due to various external factors," he says. "Our basic thinking is that if costs rise by a moderate amount, we will work to keep sales prices unchanged through measures like improving production efficiency to absorb those increased costs, and by bearing the remaining costs ourselves, to the extent possible.

"However, considering the overall profitability of the business, if the impact over the mid-to-long term is such that we cannot absorb the costs through our own efforts, and we determine that it would be difficult to maintain a healthy profit structure, we will need to consider price revisions."

When it comes to software, Furukawa says the impact is more limited. Regardless, rising component prices do impact game cards, and "the situation is not necessarily favorable either."

"Our basic policy for software is to set prices that reflect the value of each title," he adds. "Instead of setting a uniform price, we consider and determine the price on an individual basis, taking the content of each software product into account."

Hardware nerds unite, sign up to our free tech newsletter for a weekly digest of the hottest new tech, the latest gadgets on the test bench, and much more from the team at GamesRadar+.

As we reported last week, the Switch 2 price seems safe for now, as Nintendo reports it has enough memory in stock to weather the storm. Additionally, the cost of buying Nintendo's latest console was increased just earlier this year, so I imagine there's little rush or desire to do so again. Switch 2 sales may be down 37% year over year, though it's still outpacing the OG Switch and PS5 quite nicely.

I can see why a more expensive Switch 2 might be attractive to investors and, in theory, the bottom line, though you also have to consider that a lofty barrier to entry turns purchase intent from "I'll buy this now" to "I'll buy this when the price eventually goes down." Whenever that is, at this rate. As former PlayStation Shawn Layden says, "true innovation" in the industry right now is making a console cheaper, not boosting frames by however much.

#4128. Heartopia celebrates 30 million downloads with new outfits, permanent price cuts

Heartopia's rise has continued since its launch earlier this year, and the game's developer isn't slowing down with updates.

Heartopia has kicked off a new event to celebrate passing 30 million downloads. Just a couple of weeks after delivering the vintage Hollywood-themed Dreamlight Cinematics event, developer XD Games has revealed The Whimsical Tea Party, a limited-time Gilded Acorn Exhibition.

The event kicked off on Saturday, bringing some new themed content to the game.

Whimsical Tea Party’s biggest addition are the new outfits, including the Wandering Traveler, and the Duke Bunny outfits. Each outfit is available in three different colours. Another thing Heartopia events bring are building materials sets.

This one adds the Labyrinth furniture building materials set, the Hedgehog & Flamingo mallet, and the Cheshire Cat pet costume. Speaking of outfits, XD Games is dropping the in-game prices for a number of items permanently.

All original pet outfits now cost 66.7% less. Those of the Common variety will now cost 10 Souvenir Ticket Stubs, instead of the previous 30. Rare pet outfits will cost 5 Souvenir Ticket Stubs, down from 15.

If you happened to buy Common or Rare original pet outfits between July 17, 2024 and March 22, 2026, you’ll be refunded the difference. This will automatically show up in-game the next time you log in. If you instead purchased those pet outfits between March 23 and April 4, you should look forward to your refund before April 10.

Keeping with the theme of freebies, Heartopia is also celebrating surpassing 30 million downloads worldwide by giving all players a small gift package in-game. This freebie is available until May 29, so you should have enough time to claim it.

For comprehensive guidance on where to find birds, bugs, and fish, check out our Heartopia bird locations, Heartopia bug locations, and Heartopia fish locations guides. If you’re instead looking to find some wild vegetables for those cooking recipes, hit those links. And, as ever, it doesn’t hurt to see if you missed out on any Heartopia codes.

#4127. Honkai: Star Rail players are eating good, with Version 4.2 and third anniversary celebrations kicking off later this month

Honkai: Star Rail will be celebrating its third anniversary just days after it delivers a major update, and there's quite a bit to chew on in this one.

HoYoverse just wrapped up a stacked Honkai: Star Rail Special Program, delivering the one-two punch of revealing the game’s next major update, and detailing what you can expect from its third anniversary celebrations.

First off, Version 4.2, dubbed So Laughed the Masses, arrives April 22, making two characters playable, and bringing back a host of beloved characters for re-runs. The new update continues the Phantasmoon Games arc, as the story takes an especially suspect new development.

The big inciting incident of this new chapter is the reveal that whoever wins the Phantasmoon Games will also become the permanent Aeon of Elation. Meanwhile, Fulwish has invited all Supplicants to the Fulwish TV HQ to announce their intention to host a TV debate about the ultimate goal of the Phantasmoon Games.

Naturally, you’re invited, and you’ll have to overcome the challenges that await to gather more Wishpower.

Our first new arrival is Silver Wolf LV.999, with whom you should already be familiar from her Version 1 form. The difference now, of course, is that she’s getting a brand-new alternate kit, since — true to her new name — she's evolved into a Godmode Player upon reaching Level 999. Silver Wolf LV.999 is a 5-Star Imaginary character on the Path of Elation.

Her main combat trick is the ability to rack up Hidden MMR, which is what allows her to eventually activate her Cartridge and settle into the aforementioned Godmode state. While in that form, she shifts the entire battle into the virtual world, pulling in both teams into her gaming domain.

This is essentially a world under her control, which is why she can unlock a Reward Stage at the start of her turn, which lets her spawn in-game items. When picked up, these items can turn the tide of battle.

Keeping up with the ultra-gamer persona, Silver Wolf's Aha Instant strike blasts all enemies with a laser cannon, dealing massive damage. Perhaps her most interesting ability is being able to hack into the battlefield when she’s not actively on the team, something she can do when a teammate falls under enemy control.

Evanescia is the other newly-playable character, who has thus far only been an observer of the Phantasmoon Games, as well as one of the most prominent new characters we've met so far on Planarcadia. V4.2 sees the girl join the roster as a 5-Star Physical character who’s likewise on the Path of Elation. As she fights, she always accumulates Certified Banger, when she earns the title she’s able to simultaneously regenerate Energy and maintain her damage.

Evanescia’s damage continues to increase the more Certified Banger she accumulates, triggering an attack from Master Fox upon reaching a certain threshold, which deals damage to all enemies and regenerates Energy for herself. Her Elation Skill adds a bit of a performance to her kit, and is capable of hitting all enemies.

You may have noticed the Path of Elation theme in this one, so you won’t be surprised to learn that the Elation Trailblazer variant on the main playable character is also joining the team in 4.2. There’s a new weapon that starts off as a glow stick but can transform into a lightblade as you deal damage, and, yes, gain Certified Banger.

It can also turn into nunchucks, which delivers a unique flurry of attacks on all enemies surrounding the character, dealing multiple instances of damage. You can also use it to cheer for a teammate, hyping them up.

Version 4.2 Warp Events will bring back six characters. The first half will see reruns of The Dahlia, Castorice, and Firefly. The second half will give you another shot at unlocking Tribbie, Sunday, and Feixiao. What’s more, four of the game’s characters will be buffed in this update, so you may want to reconsider putting them them back on your team. They are Firefly, Huohuo, Seele, and Welt.

As part of the same update, you can expect the debut of the Cosmic Data Roaming event, which goes live alongside the anniversary celebrations. The event lets you live the life of a streamer.

Currency Wars is getting a big expansion, too. Likewise, the Cosmicon Collective is getting its version 2.0 update, adding new decks, dice as well as a new team challenge game mode.

As for the big third anniversary celebration, it will kick off in-game on April 26, bringing back Festive Gifts. The event will only be available during these celebrations, and it will once again be gifting players who log in regularly a total of 20 pulls.

You’ll also be able to a select a blessing card from a companion of your choice to receive a special gift of 1,600 Stellar Jades. The same celebrations will also seeHuohuo and Robin permanently added to the Stellar Convergence store. You’ll have another chance to exchange a Golden Companion Spirit for any companion you like in that store, too — and all you need to do is log in anytime between Versions 4.2 and 4.4. This being a new year for Honkai: Star Rail, the top-up double bonus is resetting, meaning anyone who tops up their wallet will get a hefty bonus.

Elsewhere, you’ll find new items in the Gift of Stardust Store, including a new outfit for Castorice. Between the time 4.2 launches and when the celebrations begin, you’ll be able to try your luck in Aha's Chosen: Spreading Elation Everywhere, an online event where you can leave a message for a chance to win various prizes.
