A map to the Lost Woods in Zelda Ocarina of Time Remake is something that can really help players navigate this maze-like location, as well as an explanation of what this realm is and how you're supposed to explore it. The Lost Woods in OoT is formed out of a series of crossroads, but taking the wrong path will spit you out back at the Kokiri Forest village and you'll have to begin again. However, if you can understand it, the Lost Woods is full of connections to the Zora's Domain, the Goron City, and more besides, acting as a network that can take you between distant regions fairly quickly.Below I'll explain how to explore the Lost Woods in Ocarina of Time, including a full map and guide to what you can find there. Keep in mind that some of these routes won't be usable straight away, as they require items that you'll find later on in the game.

Below is a full map for the Lost Woods in Ocarina of Time, including the different access points and points of interest you can find within.

There are multiple different access points to the Lost Woods, some of which require certain abilities. They are unlocked in the following ways:

The Lost Woods are full of dark tunnels that lead you back to Kokiri Forest if you pick them. To avoid these, you need to listen for the music and go through the tunnel that it's most clearly coming from.

If you choose right, there'll be an aura of green musical notes as you get close, as shown above. These mark the path that will lead you to the Sacred Forest Meadow and Grove, and thus the essential pathway through the Lost Woods.

#4092. 'The Best RPG I've Played This Year' - Queen's Domain Is A Low-Key GOTY Contender On Xbox

Back at the end of last month, a little-known RPG launched on Xbox in the form of Queen's Domain, which we highlighted in our October 30th new releases roundup alongside 14 other titles that arrived that day.

Ever since then, we've been hearing various bits of praise for the game across multiple platforms, and it's gotten to the point where it's definitely a Game of the Year contender - albeit a very low-key one.

Officially, what you're getting here is a "retro-fantasy action RPG with brutal combat and traversal-focused exploration", and Queen's Domain is being compared to loads of legendary franchises including King's Field, Zelda and Dark Souls.

Here's what just a few people are saying about it on Steam, for example:

cautious asparagus on Steam: "It's the kind of game that keeps surprising you with the sheer scope and creativity. You know the first time in Elden Ring where you find the elevator that brings you down to Siofra River, and you're just in awe of how much more there is to the game? There are multiple times in Queen's Domain where you feel that same way. This is the best RPG I have played this year, and it might even be my game of the year."

Huell Babineaux: "Everyone says this is one of the best kings field successors out there and it probably is, but ive never played those games, so to me this game feels more like a dark and gritty first person legend of zelda, and it pulls this off exceptionally well. Combat is brutal and unforgiving, but also learnable. Exploration can be daunting and overwhelming, but always rewarding.

Powersteve on Steam: My game of the year. Not just the best King's Field imitator but a genuine improvement on the formula. Better combat, better variety of combat options and a massive world with some of the best level and secret design I have ever seen. Also remains engaging and balanced for the whole duration and doesn't turn into Doom with lightning bolts half way through like Lunacid. So good that I can't wait to get all the endings just so I can use those secrets to do a fresh run with sequence breaks which is something that I almost never do.

So, why haven't we mentioned this before? Well, the Xbox version of Queen's Domain was actually getting a bit of flack at launch, as people were pointing out a stuttering issue that seemed to be plaguing the Series X and S versions.

Looking at the reviews on the Xbox Store now though, the issue seems to have been addressed in a recent patch, and Queen's Domain is currently rocking a 4.7/5 rating on the US version of the Xbox Store as things stand.

In other words, this might well be worth picking up for your Xbox console! It's £16.74 / $19.99 if you fancy taking a punt in the near future, and we'll leave you with more details and screenshots for it down below.

Queen’s Domain is a retro-fantasy action RPG. Washed up on the shores of the Isle of Neasied, you set out to find your father and uncover the dark heart of this mysterious isle. Wield the Legendary Holy Sword Endu to take flight from platform to platform, and discover an interconnected, labyrinthine world where secrets and dangers lurk around every corner.

Fight action-oriented battles with a classic stamina meter, powerful charge attacks, weapon specific special attacks, and secondary throwing weapons. Level up, accessorize, and choose from a huge catalogue of melee weapons on your quest to fight your way through the hordes of monsters and powerful bosses awaiting you in the darkest depths of the isle.

I love being Cyrodiil's one-man deep state in charge of all major economic, social, criminal, and paramilitary organizations.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Speaking on a new episode of The Examined Game, Skyrim lead designer Bruce Nesmith shared his big takeaway from Baldur's Gate 3, and contrasted the approaches Bethesda and Larian have taken in their respective RPGs.

"The surprises come with the little things, not the big things. I have a long history with D&D as well as Bethesda. For me, it was joyful to see the D&D expression of fantasy rules come to life. Larian Studios did a magnificent job of that. I also thought that they redefined things in a certain way. Bethesda games have always had the philosophy of, let the player play everything.

"You can play the entire Thieves' Guild, you can play the entire Fighters' Guild, you can play the entire Mages' Guild, etc. There is nothing that your character can't play. That's a very good philosophy. I support that philosophy. But I was pleasantly surprised to see how positive it felt to me to make consequential decisions that closed off gameplay in Baldur's Gate.

"That also felt good, because it was done well. I felt like the decisions I made had more meaning in certain ways, because there were actual consequences. If I wanted to see those other [outcomes], I'd have to bring up another character and try different paths.

"They were both fun, they're just fun in different ways, and that, to me, was part of the surprise. I would have expected to fall on one side or the other, as if they were things [where] you couldn't have both. The lesson learned is: You can have both. I can enjoy this game over here that does it this way, and enjoy this game over here that does it that way."

I think Nesmith is 100% correct, and it's really Bethesda's lane to offer relatively unhindered fantasy fulfillment in its games. You generally see players and modders be the ones to introduce roleplaying-oriented restrictions, while Bethesda maximizes freedom.

At the same time, I've always thought that what separates Bethesda games from more pure sim sandboxes like Mount & Blade is that the studio provides the player with just enough structure and narrative to push back on. I think there's room to experiment there, and examples in Bethesda's own back catalogue of where it can take things.

Morrowind springs to mind: The Fighters' and Thieves' Guilds are opposed to each other, and their quests are mutually exclusive after a point⁠—you even directly sabotage the other guild in each questline. The Mages' Guild and House Telvanni are similarly opposed, and the Dunmer Houses pretty much all hate each other.

But you don't even have to go all the way back to 2002: Skyrim has three major examples in the Civil War questline, the Dawnguard expansion, and the alternate ending to the Dark Brotherhood story. Siding with the Penitus Oculatus in "Destroy the Dark Brotherhood" isn't as substantial as the faction quest you're throwing away, but it is a very cool addition that enhances Skyrim's sense of depth and stakes. I'd love to see more like it in TES6: Sentinel⁠—wouldn't it be rad to have a full questline for both the secret police and the assassins' guild?

I caught on Nesmith's choice of words that he enjoyed Baldur's Gate 3's approach "because it was done well." I've certainly encountered content-blocking choices in games that felt cheap or forced. I'm a huge CD Projekt fan, but I'll always be a hater when it comes to The Witcher 2's mutually exclusive second acts. I think the same idea was executed much better in Cyberpunk 2077: Phantom Liberty.

#4088. Zelda: Ocarina Of Time "Off To A Great Start", Says Nintendo

Nintendo has released the Q&A translation from its latest financial briefing, with president Shuntaro Furukawa stating that Zelda: Ocarina of Time is "off to a great start".

The comment comes off the back of a question related to the decrease in hardware sales for the Switch 2, which saw a dip of 37% year-on-year. Furukawa-san explained that Japan saw a significant spike in sales prior to the price revision in May before settling down after. Overseas, meanwhile, Nintendo allowed customers ample time to purchase the Switch 2 before the price went up while also offering multiple bundles.

With the release of the Zelda 40th Anniversary console, Furukawa-san said that this "contributed to strong sales in various regions". At the time of the Q&A, he explains that while it's too early to provide specific figures for Ocarina of Time, the game is off to a great start, with Nintendo in good shape for the coming holiday season.

Nintendo usually holds off on providing specific sales figures until its quarterly financial briefings, so it's possible we might not know how well Ocarina of Time sold for a little while yet. That said, if it's performing particularly well, it's equally likely that Nintendo will provide a separate announcement via its investor relations page and social media accounts. We'll keep an eye out either way.

For the UK at least, we know that the physical release was the second-biggest in series history, beating Breath of the Wild yet falling short of Tears of the Kingdom, with the Switch's high install base likely a big factor for the latter. As for console sales, Nintendo is maintaining its current forecast of 16 million total sales for the fiscal year.

#4087. PS5 Now the Only Console without a Digital Game Gifting Option

If even a Nintendo platform has a digital storefront feature and you don't, then you truly are behind the times. The firm notoriously playing catch-up in this space has today confirmed the Nintendo eShop will be receiving the ability to gift digital games.

The PS Store, which will eventually be the only place you can buy new PlayStation games, still doesn't allow it.

Having downloaded a new system update for the Nintendo Switch 2, the groundwork is laid for a Nintendo eShop gifting feature going live next week. You will be able to gift digital games to people within your Nintendo Account family group.

This implementation is a bit more restrictive than what's on Xbox and Steam, where you can gift digital games to anyone on your friends list. The Nintendo Account family group system, meanwhile, is restricted to a maximum of eight members that all share a single online membership to NSO (Nintendo Switch Online).

Despite the Nintendo approach being less expansive than other storefronts, it's better than nothing.

And nothing is all Sony offers in the digital game gifting space.

Feature 8 Ways Sony Must Improve the PS Store for Our All-Digital Future

From January 2028, PlayStation is going entirely digital with game releases, as it's revealed the production of physical copies for new titles will end. As it leans all the way into the digital space, it makes the PS Store the only place you can buy new PS5 (and potentially PS6 by that point) games.

This has put the PS Store under the microscope, as players now judge the only storefront they'll be able to access new PlayStation releases from. The fact that, as of right now, they wouldn't be able to gift games to their family and friends, is an issue. And now, if the Nintendo Switch 2 can support the feature, there are absolutely no excuses Sony can turn to.

It's one improvement we highlighted in a recent feature that PlayStation really should implement. Other enhancements included a better refund policy, the ability to trade and sell digital games, and a loyalty program.

Currently, the only way you could send a PS5, PS4 game to a family member or friend is by buying them PSN vouchers to redeem. By choosing to focus entirely on digital in the future, Sony must implement a gifting feature where the full process is done entirely on the console.

What do you make of this? Post your thoughts in the comments below.

#4086. Nintendo's Analysis Indicates You Might Want To Watch The Zelda Movie With Others

The Legend of Zelda movie is fast approaching, scheduled to release on 30th April 2027 (we could really do with a trailer soon, Nintendo).

A such, we felt it only right to relay a new quote from Nintendo's latest financial Q&A session. While it may seem obvious to some (and perplexing to others), it seems that the best way to experience Nintendo's movies is to watch them with friends and/or family. In other words, if you want to have more fun, maybe don't go on your own.

This comes specifically from Yusuke Beppu, corporate director and member of the board at Nintendo. He explains that the company surveyed the satisfaction levels of viewers who watched The Super Mario Galaxy Movie and found that the levels "were higher when people watched in groups of two instead of alone, and higher still when watched in groups of four instead of groups of two".

"I want to mention that when we surveyed the satisfaction levels of people who watched The Super Mario Galaxy Movie, we found that these levels were higher when people watched in groups of two instead of alone, and higher still when watched in groups of four instead of groups of two. As illustrated by the four controller ports on Nintendo 64 in the past, Nintendo has long placed value on the idea of everyone playing together.”

Of course, despite Nintendo's findings, we want to stress that you're free to enjoy movies in whatever manner you deem suitable. Going to the cinema on your own can be a joyous experience, so if that's how you want to experience the new Zelda movie, then don't let Nintendo (or us!) convince you otherwise.

Nintendo also once again reiterated its desire to make more movies beyond Zelda. Beppu-san explained that movies "allow us to convey the appeal of Nintendo's uniquenessand characters in a concentrated 90- or 120-minute experience", while also providing an opportunity for its developers to learn new skills.

News Nintendo To Continue Delivering Movies Beyond Live-Action Zelda, Unsurprisingly

News Nintendo Excited About Broadening Zelda's Audience With Live-Action Movie

"That's one of the most exciting things for us"

#4085. Poll: Xbox Turns 25 This Week, But Which Console Generation Had The Best Launch Titles?

This Sunday, Xbox will celebrate 25 years of great games and console experiences. Without giving away just how ancient we are, Fraser and I have been Xbox players since the beginning, enjoying each new generation of Xbox consoles and the games that launched alongside them.

With November 15th drawing closer, we thought we'd look back on each generation's launch lineup and ask for your verdict: which Xbox console had the best launch titles?

Was it the original Xbox, with Halo: Combat Evolved, Project Gotham Racing, and Fuzion Frenzy? How about the Xbox 360, with Condemned: Criminal Origins, Kameo: Elements of Power, and Call of Duty 2? Perhaps the Xbox One, with Ryse: Son of Rome, Dead Rising 3, and Forza Motorsport 5? Or is it the Xbox Series X|S, with Gears Tactics, Forza Horizon 4, and Sea Of Thieves?

We all have our favourite games from each console generation, but which one had the best launch lineup? That's for you to decide by voting in the poll below. Before you do, though, here's a closer look at each Xbox generation's launch titles:

On this page: Poll: Xbox Turns 25 This Week, But Which Console Generation Had The Best Launch Titles?

So, now you know which games launched with which Xbox consoles, and all that's left to do is vote! I reckon I can probably guess which console the PX community will favour, but who knows? Get voting!

As reported by Axios, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has admitted to carrying on an extramarital affair with Alice Huang, an executive at Singaporean cloud computing company, Megaspeed. According to The New York Times, the Trump administration suspects Ms. Huang of passing information to China's Ministry of State Security. The Chinese government denies the accusation.

Both the NYT and Financial Times' previous reporting on Jensen Huang pursuing a romantic relationship with Alice Huang were contested by Nvidia, which had maintained that any relationship between the two was strictly professional.

Axios obtained a draft version of Jensen Huang's email apology to Nvidia employees. "I owe my family and all of you an apology," Huang allegedly wrote. "I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did." Huang reportedly took "full responsibility" for the affair, but will not step down as Nvidia's CEO: "I am fully committed to Nvidia and will work to earn back your confidence."

Nvidia's board is organizing an independent committee to investigate the relationship, but does not believe company or national security secrets were compromised. Nvidia's board is not seeking Huang's removal from the CEO position.

This all comes as the US takes an increasingly hawkish stance toward China, framing AI development as a national security issue and restricting the sale of advanced AI chips to Chinese companies. Meanwhile, US-based AI companies and their aggressive datacenter buildouts are proving increasingly unpopular with American voters.

I think I speak for all of us when I say: Damn, that's crazy. Remember when Jensen Huang was just the gaming graphics guy and not the AI apocalypse national security guy? Perhaps we were all happier in those simpler times, including Huang, whatever his skyrocketing net worth might say to the contrary.

#4083. Mini Review: Warhammer Survivors (PS5) - Absurdly Addictive Crossover Is a Match Made in Bullet Hell

Warhammer Survivors is exactly what its name suggests: a Warhammer reskin of Vampire Survivors.

Developed by licensed Warhammer studio Auroch Digital, with Vampire Survivors creator poncle partnering on the project, it's a fantastic, heartfelt adaptation right out of the gate.

Indeed, it's immediately obvious that an awful lot of care has been taken in providing poncle's world-beating gameplay formula with a fresh coat of paint. The Warhammer settings, characters, enemies, and weapons are all there — but the game also relishes in dishing out smaller references to Games Workshop's immensely popular fiction.

In particular, I was left pleasantly surprised by how often Warhammer Survivors pays tribute to the property's tabletop identity. Numerous playable characters, for example, are unlocked by finding miniature figure paints scattered across maps.

Meanwhile, power ups can include rolling damage dice — actual dice — across the battlefield, crushing your foes in the process. You can even drop giant blast radius templates on top of your enemies if you're lucky.

What I'm saying is that Auroch Digital and poncle clearly had loads of fun with this one — it's not just a simple copy and paste job that takes advantage of the Warhammer name.

Oh, and it's basically two games in one. On the main menu, you can pick between Warhammer's dark sci-fi 40,000 setting, and its high fantasy Age of Sigmar setting. Each comes with its own character roster, maps, enemy factions, objectives, upgrades, and everything else, making for a seriously robust package.

Gameplay-wise, the title offers a slight twist on the absurdly addictive Survivors structure. Stages have a 25-minute time limit instead of 30, and I'd say there's a larger emphasis on tactical thinking.

That's because specialised opponents are more prevalent, forcing you to weave your way through the hordes in a more methodical manner. At least, until you rack up so many super-powered upgrades that anything in your path just evaporates anyway.

Yep, that same progression curve that makes Vampire Survivors so insanely moreish is alive and well here, although I do think it takes a little longer to hit those truly chaotic highs because of the aforementioned tweaks.

All in all, Warhammer Survivors perfectly melds Games Workshop's property with poncle's timeless formula, resulting in another exceptional roguelike experience.

#4082. New Details Revealed About The Physical Edition Of GTA 6 For Xbox Series X|S

Double-sided poster, shipping dates & more

Everyone already knows about the code-in-a-box situation for GTA 6's physical edition on Xbox Series X|S and PS5, but we've also come to learn a few extra details in recent days about what to expect from the boxed copy of the game.

So, when you open up GTA 6 for Xbox Series X|S in physical form, you'll be presented with a code that will allow you to redeem the game on the Microsoft Store - essentially converting your physical purchase into a digital one.

Rockstar Games mentioned a shipping date of November 12th for the physical version a few days ago, but we've spotted some retailers saying they'll start shipping on the 11th instead, while a very small number of people even seem to have their copy already.

Once you've got the physical version in your hands, you'll be able to preload GTA 6 in full, although you can technically also do that from tonight by installing the game via the Xbox mobile app.

As you can also see from the tweet above, the physical edition is now confirmed to come with a double-sided A3 poster (at least if you buy from certain retailers). This poster appears to include the game's main artwork along with some character art on the back, so that's at least a nice little bonus to ease the pain of a disc-less release.

But what about a map? Well, Rockstar Games is handling the map a bit differently this time around, making a digital version available to download for free at launch. Alternatively, physical maps will be available to buy from the Rockstar Store "shortly after launch" for $0.99, but we reckon those will be in extreme demand and quickly sell out.

Of course, none of this really changes the fact that the physical edition of GTA 6 is kinda pointless for any platform as things stand, but it does at least make for a good display piece, and it'll be popular for gifting purposes this Christmas.

What's even weirder about this is that Rockstar is supporting GTA 6's launch with various other physical releases, such as an official soundtrack album and all kinds of merch, but it seems there's little hope for a disc version right now.

#4081. Mini Review: Pikmin 4 - Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy (Switch 2) - Pleasant But Perplexingly Piecemeal

The latest addition to the pantheon of obscenely long-titled Nintendo Switch 2 Editions is a strange one. Pikmin 4 - Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy takes the Switch 1 game that I have long considered ripe for a new hardware touch-up and does...not a lot with it. It's a chance to revisit one of Nintendo's finest games from the last generation, and the upgrade's price of admission (£7.99 / $9.99) is admittedly a small one, but on the 'new' front, I'm left wanting more.

Let's start with the usual 'Switch 2 Edition' bells and whistles. Pikmin 4 now plays in stunning native 4K resolution docked, and there's added GameShare support for those who want to play some cross-console Dandori Battles with a pal.

If you ask me, Pikmin 4 was already one of the best-looking titles on Switch 1, and the resolution bump doesn't feel transformative. That said, there's no denying that it's even more of a looker on the newer hardware.

Review Pikmin 4 (Switch) - Relaxed, Refined Real-Time Strategy, Ready To Crack The Mainstream

Strangely, the typical Switch 2 givens of a 60fps boost and Mouse Mode are not included this time around. While the former is disappointing, the latter downright confuses me. Nintendo has crowbarred this control scheme in everywhere, but it's absent from a game with a stick-controlled pointer? Even in the co-op Pebble Pitcher mode? Madness!

There's also a new Howl-Out feature that lets you shout commands to Oatchi via the Switch 2 microphone. It's a sweet, if occasionally inconsistent, little bonus that I quickly turned off after realising my real-world dog was getting miffed at me shouting "Good Pup!" without giving him a stroke on the head.

The big newbie is the titular Dandori Academy, where you're tasked with clearing a stage's treasure as quickly as possible. You practice during the week, then take a weekend 'exam', unlocking various medals and in-game rewards in the process. The Dandori stages were a highlight of the base game, and it's great to have even more of them to play here. The three difficulty options provide a welcome challenge in the later stages, and with 72 of them arriving over the next year, it's a wonderful excuse to return to one of my favourite Switch 1 games.

The mode's rollout, however, is a little confusing. 72 new stages sound great on paper, but that means only six new challenges are available each month. If you happen to ace most of them on the first exam weekend, you're left with three weeks of nothing new. Sure, it gives me a prime reason to come back to Pikmin 4 on the regular in 2027, but it does leave things feeling rather slight at launch.

Overall, £8/$10 is a small price to pay for some minor new features and a fun little mode that'll keep me entertained over the coming year, but it's more of a budding shoot right now than the full-bloom upgrade I had dreamed of.

#4080. Marvel fans want James Gunn back after his DC departure: "Start drafting the script for Guardians of the Galaxy 4"

Join the GamesRadar community for quick access. Enter your email below and we'll send confirmation, and sign you up to our newsletter.

Marvel fans want James Gunn back in the MCU

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

After four years, James Gunn is stepping down as DC Studios co-CEO alongside Peter Safran, but Marvel fans are taking this as a win, as many want the Guardians of the Galaxy director to come back to the MCU.

"Kevin Feige, it's time to bring James Gunn back into the fold," said one fan on Reddit just hours after the news broke. Others seem to agree, as another added, "The people acting like Gunn is awful and don’t want him returning to Marvel are fucking crazy. All three Guardians of the Galaxy movies are great, and he was a great second or third unit director to have on hand for the bigger projects. You’d be crazy to not welcome him back. He has still done cosmic Marvel the best when it comes to the movies."

One fan on Twitter let Gunn know exactly what he should do next, writing, "start drafting the script for Guardians of the Galaxy 4." Another said, "James Gunn no longer DC head means Guardians of the Galaxy 4 confirmed at Marvel?" Let's go."

Gunn started working with Marvel in 2012 when he was hired to co-write and direct the first Guardians of the Galaxy, which was released in 2014. The filmmaker went on to direct scenes in Doctor Strange and wrote and directed the second Guardians movie. However, just as he was slated to direct the third movie, Disney fired Gunn from Marvel Studios in 2018 due to resurfaced social media posts.

Gunn was rehired by Marvel in 2019 and later directed Guardians of the Galaxy Vol.3. But he slowly made the jump to DC, writing and directing the 2021 movie The Suicide Squad and then the HBO show Peacemaker. Then in 2022, Gunn was made co-CEO of DC Studios alongside his long-term collaborator Safran. However, with Gunn now stepping down as DC boss, perhaps the filmmaker will jump ship again.

The DC shake-up comes after Skydance acquired Warner Bros. earlier this year. Gunn and Safran will be replaced by former Marvel Studios executive Jeremy Latcham on December 1, 2026. In a statement posted on Instagram, Gunn said he feels relieved and that he "disliked the at-times corporate nature of the job" and had "difficulty" with "dividing my time between projects" and his role as CEO.

Gunn only launched the DCU: Chapter One with Superman last year. Though reports suggest that the DCU will be dismantled, it looks like projects that are currently in the works will still go forward, including Man of Tomorrow, The People v. Gorilla Grodd, and Creature Commandos season 2.

For more, check out our guide on how to watch the DC movies in order, and keep up with upcoming DC movies and shows announced before Gunn's departure.

CEO Mike Bilder doesn't see AI as having much to offer Jackbox.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

On a recent visit to Jackbox Games HQ here in Chicago, I got to speak with developers and studio leadership about their process, history, and place in the industry. Given, you know, everything, I'm pretty much contractually obligated to ask about AI in conversations like this. Here's what CEO Mike Bilder had to say on the topic:

"The people are what make this product. The comedy, the writing, and the art, all that is done by people, and we have no intention of changing that. I don't think we're experts on what's going on with AI in the industry and any of that. There's obviously uses for tooling and for research, and [for] all that kind of stuff [AI is] incredibly powerful.

"But from a generative asset standpoint, we don't have any intention of replacing people, or people-made editorial and art with it."

From everything we had discussed up to this point, as well as Jackbox's whole deal, I didn't think generative AI would really be in the cards for the studio. But I still appreciated Bilder's straightforward, clear answer on the subject, particularly when the standard playbook these days is fence sitting reminiscent of The Simpsons' "Abortions for some, miniature American flags for others."

Jackbox's games are relatively lightweight from a tech perspective, while the art and writing is their main draw⁠—if anything was noticeably AI-generated, it would put the value of the whole package into question.

The company recently released the Jackbox Party Pack 12 on October 14, and the studio's production values have really progressed since the last entry I had played⁠—Trivia Murder Party 3 makes extensive use of realtime 3D graphics, for example. Jackbox Party Pack 12 is available on pretty much everything, but this is Personal Computer Gamer, so I'll say you can grab it on Steam.

#4077. Dedicated PS5, PS5 Pro Patch Aims to Fix Silent Hill 2 Graphics Issues

Could the excellent Silent Hill 2 remake finally be fixed on base PS5 and PS5 Pro? That's what a new patch for the game seems to be suggesting.

A new update for the survival horror remake, dedicated entirely to PS5 and PS5 Pro, is live now, bringing it up to version 1.08. The patch notes speak of addressing all the graphical issues that have quietly plagued the game for months now.

Having installed the new update, you should discover "numerous fixes" relating to the "lighting, shadows, and reflections [issues] that were occurring in multiple locations". Both of the Performance and Quality modes have been patched with consistency improvements, and the flickering in water surfaces, lighting effects, and reflections has been "corrected".

While these were not major problems, the patch also improves the cutscenes in certain places and fixes a glitch where you wouldn't be able to obtain some items.

The issues surrounding Silent Hill 2 — the PS5 Pro version in particular — date all the way back to a month after the original release. At the time, Bloober Team was aware of the problems and a patch was being worked on. The update didn't work, and eventually, the responsibility shifted to publisher Konami. More updates followed, and now today's new patch 1.08 directly targets PS5 and PS5 Pro fixes.

#4076. Review: Metaphor: ReFantazio (Switch 2) - An Extraordinary JRPG That Could Use Another Optimisation Pass

A game with the name 'Metaphor' that tackles issues such as culture diversity, democracy, and classism isn't exactly subtle in its delivery, but is just as poignant in 2026 as it was when the game first released in 2024.

Atlus has brought its critically acclaimed turn-based role-playing to Switch 2, and in doing so, reminded everyone of two things: That Atlus are absolute masters at delivering striking stories, endearing characters, and engaging combat through the lens of an incredibly unique art style, and that optimisation for handheld consoles is not their strong suit.

Metaphor: ReFantazio is simultaneously the story of a young boy yearning to reconnect with his dear friend, the prince of the kingdom of Euchronia who had been struck with a curse that left him in a comatose state, a story of prejudice and social manipulation through the kingdom itself, started by the assassination of the king at the hands of Louis Guiabarn, a common-born army officer wanting to challenge the status quo through true meritocracy, AND the story of the parallels between fantasy and reality, using real-life situations as elements of idealistic fantasy within Metaphor's world, things that could never happen for the residents of Euchronia.

The way that Metaphor deftly handles so many threads of varying sizes and scopes is nothing short of extraordinary, especially when the themes of anxiety, willpower, and hope are so striking in the real world.

The individual characters in Metaphor are largely brilliantly written, with their own struggles and demons to battle, even if they aren't party members or sometimes even less important to the overarching plot. Characters like the bat-like Eugief, Heismay, battles prejudice for his race whilst trying to mourn the loss of a family member, but displays his own prejudice against the rabbit-like Papirus for their part in his grief. The stoic Brigitta, owner of the capital's magic igniter shop, casts an icy exterior, only to show her true colours through a puppy she can't resist but take in.

Even the game's main antagonist, Louis, is incredibly compelling, bringing an immediate presence to the screen through his striking design and charismatic dialogue, but as is par for the course, there is far more than meets the eye with Louis. There are a lot of plates to spin in Metaphor, but almost all of them are tantalising events to keep returning to.

It's difficult not to make comparisons between Studio Zero's Metaphor and the Persona series, as they share a lot of DNA: a calendar-based system that has you not only exploring dungeons for treasure and boss fights, but also balancing improvement of social stats, or virtues as they're known here, and bonds with party members and other important NPCs to learn more of their personal stories and gain benefits to the more traditional JRPG aspects of the game in the process.

But Metaphor stands alone in Atlus' repertoire by not only drawing from Persona, but the core Shin Megami Tensei franchise as well, while infusing its own flair in its combat mechanics through the Archetype system.

Archetypes in Metaphor are much closer to the Final Fantasy series' job system than they are to Persona, with each character gaining skills and masteries through use of interchangeable classes gained through the social parts of the game, and combat-earned AP gained to level them up. MAG, a currency gained through both combat and socialisation, can be used to transfer skills from one archetype to another, giving you plenty of ways to experiment with your own builds between the seven party members and the 30 different Archetypes alone.

Combat itself utilises the Turn Icon system resembling core Shin Megami Tensei games, with extra actions gained by striking a critical hit or weakness, or serious losses by missing an attack or hitting an absorbed element. You can also strike at an advantage by attacking enemies in the overworld in real-time, or take them out entirely if you're high enough above them in level (a feature I wish all future JRPGs would carry!), but if an enemy gets the jump on you, it can be devastating. All of these elements combine to make arguably the best combat Atlus has ever put out in a JRPG.

It's also impossible to discuss the game without mentioning its frankly stellar soundtrack. Composer Shoji Meguro's unique flavour is felt throughout the game, with one of the best battle themes to ever grace a JRPG, drawing from Buddhist sutra inspirations with priest Keisuke Honryo's unforgettable chanting.

All of this is to say that Metaphor: ReFantazio is an incredible JRPG, and one that will keep you coming back over and over for well over 80 hours. However, on Switch 2, the experience hasn't come across without a few hiccups along the way.

After releasing Persona 3 Reload on Switch 2 last year, which itself suffered greatly from frame rate issues and muddy visuals, and experiencing inconsistencies with Metaphor: ReFantazio itself in its original release, I was sceptical, to say the least, and that scepticism ended up having merit, as I'm not sure I've seen a game look quite so beautiful and hideous at the same time!

From an artistic standpoint, Metaphor is sumptuous, taking the 'more is more' approach from Persona and applying a much wider colour palette; the UI and menus are stunning, of that there's no doubt. But technically speaking, Metaphor is a bit of a mess.

There are options to run in performance, balanced, or graphics modes both handheld and docked, but regardless of which mode you pick, there were inconsistencies throughout. One moment in combat could look stunning AND run well, and the next cutscene you'd encounter the strangest case of anti-aliasing and fuzzy textures, despite there only being two characters in the room.

Frame rate issues also persist regardless of performance or graphics settings, never enough to overtake the other amazing qualities of the game, but always enough to notice and occasionally distract. Persona 3 Reload did eventually get a performance update that fixed a lot of issues; suffice it to say, I truly hope Metaphor gets one as well!

Additionally, while so much of Metaphor's main dungeons and set pieces are a sight to behold, Atlus's dungeon designs have often left something to be desired, and that's apparent in Metaphor's side dungeons. When on a side quest, it's fairly easy to get turned around in the sea of brown tunnels and foggy forest areas, simply on the back of them all looking identical! It's a stark difference to the Regalith Cathedral, Sandworm's Belly, or Skyrunner main dungeons, for sure.

Metaphor: ReFantazio is an extraordinary JRPG, juggling stories and systems alike with grace and effortlessness, but it is let down somewhat by poor optimisation on Switch 2.

Anyone looking for a huge, sprawling adventure with lovable characters, compelling parallels to the real world, and progression systems that will keep you coming back for more will be far from disappointed with this game, but there's no metaphor for a dodgy frame rate and visuals that can occasionally take you out of the fantasy.

#4075. Feature: These Are Xbox's Best 25 Games From 2001-2026 According To Metacritic

As we continue our celebrations for Xbox's 25th anniversary this Sunday (November 15th), we thought it might be fun to look back at the past 25 years on Metacritic, and specifically the best-rated Xbox games from each year.

The website has a significant history of review roundups dating all the way back to 2001, and looking at the list, the early years in particular are jam-packed with historic Xbox games! Halo is in there multiple times, as is Gears of War and Grand Theft Auto, and then we start to see an indie explosion with the likes of Inside and Hades in later years.

So, here are Xbox's best 25 games from 2001-2026 according to Metacritic from each individual year. Just keep in mind that we've eliminated a couple of expansions, as we're only counting full game releases.

Of course, when it comes to 2026 specifically, there's every chance GTA 6 will end up taking the top spot within a couple of weeks' time, so just keep that in mind - Hades 2 has done amazingly well, but will most likely be surpassed.

And by the way, this list doesn't tell the full story - here's what it would look like if you took the individual years away:

Pretty different, right? It's no surprise that there were multiple years that fared better than others in terms of highly-rated releases, so the likes of The Orange Box, Red Dead Redemption 2, Portal 2, Halo 3 and others still make the lineup.

Anyway, Metacritic doesn't tell the full story by any means here, but it's a useful resource to look back and see how well the critics positioned these games at the time, and whether we reckon they're still justifying their high scores.

So, what do you reckon to these? We'd love to hear your thoughts down in the comments section below.

Guide The Best Original Xbox Games Of All Time

Including exclusives & backwards compatible titles

Fraser is the News Editor at Pure Xbox, where he spends his time reporting on the biggest stories in the world of Xbox and beyond.

There is undoubtedly a time when review scores became more inline with the scores we see today. In other words, there is no way that Halo: Combat Evolved would score 97 under todays review score regime. Don't misunderstand me, Halo: CE is still a great game, but if reviewed today it would be marked down for its samey locations, limited enemy types etc. etc. (and I just picked that game, rather than picking on that game).

I wonder when that would have been? Any thoughts, @FraserG?

Does the passing of each generation further refine the scores that professional reviewers give, and I wonder what those same games would be given if reviewed today...?

I don't think there's any guarantee that gta6 gets a higher average review than 95, so Hades 2 may well end the year with top spot.

@Fiendish-Beaver I think about this a lot. Really, only Nintendo games can break the 95 barrier now.

When you look at gears e day that kind of content is probably a 93 if we go back 15 years

@Llamageddon Yeah, 95 is a tough score to beat. It could be tight for R* to contend with that.

@Fiendish-Beaver I agree with the Halo point. I think a lot of games back then got a lot of praise due to the graphical jumps between generations. I mean, 16bit > 32bit was ridiculously jaw-dropping. The same can be said about 64bit > 128bit. I think many games from the Xbox / PS2 / Gamecube era wowed more than impressed. We don't really see that today, do we? Generational jumps just seem so slight (when we compare games at the end of one gen to the beginning of the next). That said, Halo 4 is the best Halo for me, followed by 1, then 2, then ODST. Halo 3 can go kick rocks. That game sucked.

Hey, @Kaloudz. Nice to see you around. Hope you are well, matey.

I agree, it was probably the wow factor that saw games receive such high scores back when gaming was much younger, and I suspect that by early in the Xbox One / PS3 era (so probably 2015ish) we had experienced much of what there was to see, and so we moved from wow to technicality. We started to judge games more on performance and variety, their technical achievement and overall enjoyment. I'd say we don't judge games based on their graphical prowess because otherwise all these retro style games would be marked down severely, which obviously does not happen.

Gains in consoles are so incremental these days that I think a game that released from 2015 onwards is probably judged by much the same standards now as it was back then.

What would be interesting, would be for someone to take up reviewing games, and to review older games but by todays standards. So someone that had never played the first Gears of War, plays it through, and gives it a review score based not on the wow, but on its technical achievements, level design, enemy variety, and what have you. I imagine that we would see a very different set of scores if games were reviewed now from what they were given when they originally released, but it would be interesting to see just how these older games would fair...

@Fiendish-Beaver I agree it is harder to get to that 95ish score than it was. I think there's a few different things going on there.

Firstly as @Kaloudz said there was a big graphical jump between generations. But there was also much larger GAMEPLAY jumps back then too. Games and their mechanics were often breaking new paradigms whether that was Mario or Zelda in 3D for the first time or Gears and Halo pushing third and third person console shooters into the mainstream on console. It felt exciting. Now most games feel much more iterative, especially AAA games.

There were also typically fewer reviews for each game, and those reviews were generally from a smaller cross-section of gamers in similar demographics who were more likely to have similar tastes, that led to homogenisation of some scores. Now a game might be marked down by a new demographic, which is fair enough, aggregate scores don't tell the whole story, we all like different things.

Linked to that I know some people believe that Nintendo games get unfairly scored higher than they might for some reason, but I don't see it that way. I think there is often a universal joy to Nintendo games that resonates with far more players. More simply put: they haven't forgotten how to make their games joyful and fun on an almost primal level. That won't be for everyone - nothing is - but it is for a wider cross section of people, and reviewers, hence they are more likely to score higher as an aggregate.

Look at Ocarina of Time remake. Not only a hit with critics currently scoring 96 on Metacritic from 94 reviews but also currently a 9.6 from 10.5k user reviews, it's rare to see both critics and users in such harmony. Having swallowed it whole and finished it already, I would agree it's the easiest 10 in years imho. Bring on GTA6.

As for the list as you'd expect with a best of list it's wall to wall bangers. I'm surprised there's more games than I thought on that list I haven't played yet, but I really struggle to start 100+ hour games like Persona 5 or BG3. One day!

BG3 is such a good game, @themightyant. Take it from someone that has been playing games for over 50 years, BG3 is the best game ever made. I have played through it multiple times now, and have amassed over 1000 hours in the game, and there are probably still things that I have not seen...

@Fiendish-Beaver Oh i'll get to it. I have no doubt, and it's not through lack of interest either. I just struggle to start games that I know will take me 100+ hours... and this one probably 200+ hours. (FYI your 1000 hours isn't helping!!! lol)

I love self employment, flexibility of work hours, but when I REALLY get into a game I often make poor life choices, and work or life suffers with no one looking over my shoulder. That is fine for something like Ocarina of Time remake - book Thursday and Friday off and finish it across 4 days, it's not that long and doesn't really impact my life.

But for games like Elden Ring, BG3, CyberPunk etc. that I pretty much KNOW I will fall head over heels into and at least partially no-life for weeks I need to be very careful when I start them. Pretty much all my most want to play games fall into this group sadly. I have at least twenty 100+ hour games near the top of my backlog.

Yes, sorry, @themightyant. I do occasionally forget that people do not have the luxury of time that I enjoy these days. If I want to game 8 hours a day every day for a fortnight that is something I could easily do (I don't, but I could).

It is a big time commitment, of that there is no doubt, and I totally understand what you mean when you say you find it off-putting because that is precisely why I have not played Assassin's Creed: Valhalla, and why I may not end up playing Crimson Desert, both of which I own, but neither of which I have played. I'd like to play them, but in the case of Valhalla, I worry I will get bored towards the end, which is what happened with both Odyssey and Origins, both of which I never finished despite putting over 100 into each of them. In the case of Crimson Desert, it feels like they keep adding to the game, and so I don't know when to start it because I will probably only want to play it once, but also want it to be feature complete by which time it will probably be to daunting to start.

If it helps, I think my 1000 hours in BG3 is divided over 4 different runs in the game. It is probably possible to complete it in under 200 hours, and that should enable you to see everything outside different story choices. According to howlongtobeat.com BG3 should take you around 180 hours if you do both mains and sides, though different choices can change the game pretty drastically...

@Fiendish-Beaver Strangely I have less concerns over something like AC: Valhalla because although it's long I know I would get a bit bored and can put it down. It's unlikely to grip me in the same way.

The problem is games I fall completely in love with and I end up staying up till the birds are tweeting, or trying to fit a few hours play into the work day.

For me it's Elden Ring, BG3, Cyberpunk, FF7 Rebirth, Persona, KCD, Hades, Monster Hunter, Death Stranding, MGSV, Metaphor re:F, Xenoblades... plenty of lengthy RPGs in fact. I'm pretty certain these will all pull me under for a while. Can't do it when I have big projects on, which is most of the time.

@themightyant I'd say Hades is quite a bit shorter than most on that list, I got to the 'true ending' in less than 50 runs and I did about half those runs in around the 20 mins mark. The platinum does extend it quite considerably though and can be a bit of a grind (if you're an achievement hunter). I would also thoroughly recommend the game (one of my personal all time favourites).

@Llamageddon You are right if they have a 30 FPS tax…. GTA6 might be low 90’s

@AlwaysPlaying also giving gta6 an 8 out of 10 (when most are giving it 10s) would drive a lot of traffic to that review even if it was pure rage baiting. I like to think all reviewers have the integrity to not do that but I'm not naive enough to believe that's the case.

Those times when you are up until ridiculous hours are some of the best gaming moments we have, @themightyant, albeit I know they are usually to be avoided.

One of my favourite memories in gaming is playing Horde in Gears 3 with 4 of my mates, with the game finally ending at 4 a.m., and whilst I know that is not particularly late (in terms of what we are talking about) the host had to be up at 5 a.m. in order to go to work! We still wax lyrical about that to this day, and that was well over 10 years ago now.

I've lost count of the days in which I started gaming in an evening only to suddenly realise there is daylight outside! I don't do it very often these days, but when it happens it does usually mean you are playing something worthwhile...

@Fiendish-Beaver They certainly are, but gaming is a privilege and life has to come first. I'll get there one day!

@Llamageddon Appreciate that. I was basing it off the HLTB times which is around 100+ hours for Hades, and I am always slower than what they say. When I love a game I usually try and complete it. Will get to it soon no doubt. I've played and loved all their other games from Bastion to Pyre and Transistor.

@themightyant absolutely, supergiant is one of my favourite small Devs, great consistency and variety. Look forward to what they cook up next (as much as I love the Hades games, they have too much talent to be stuck making one series).

#4074. Guide: Cyberpunk 2077: Best Mods on PS5

What are the best Cyberpunk 2077 mods on PS5? In this guide, I'm going to highlight which mods I think are well worth installing to make your dark future experience more enticing.

On this page: Cyberpunk 2077: Best Mods on PS5

Mod support for Cyberpunk 2077 was added with Patch 2.5 on PS5, allowing for user-created content on Sony's console.

Choosing and installing mods is easy: just click the 'Mods' option on the game's main menu and you'll be taken to the current list of available mods. You can scroll through pages manually or you can use the search bar.

If you find a mod you like, select it from the list and then click the 'Install' button, or just press the Options button on your controller to install it right there and then.

You can also hit the 'Like' button to add the mod to your 'Liked' list. Doing this lets you keep track of your favourite mods via the 'Liked' filter button new the top of the screen.

You can have a maximum of 150 mods installed at any one time, and said mods need to have a combined file size of 15.76GB or under (although this isn't really an issue as of yet, as standard mod sizes tend to be very, very small).

Unfortunately, yes, using any mods disables Trophies when playing Cyberpunk 2077 on PS5.

This counts for any save file that has ever been used in conjunction with mods.

As such, you may want to beat the game at least once, or go all the way and get the Platinum, before diving into the world of mods.

Below, you'll find a list of what I think are currently the best Cyberpunk 2077 mods available on PS5.

Admittedly, the selection is far from vast at this point in time — but new mods are being added on what seems to be a weekly basis, and so this list should only grow over the coming months.

A mod that's bound to be at or near the top of Cyberpunk 2077's modding menu for years to come, Deceptious Quest Core is a necessary framework mod for a number of Deceptious' other mods.

Basically, you need to have this mod installed if you want a few of the other mods featured on this list — it's just the way that the game's quest-based modding works.

Any mod that has [DQC] in its title requires Quest Core to function.

Note that you need to enter V's H10 apartment (and then possibly exit it) for this mod to activate, and subsequently activate all of the [DQC] mods.

This mod aims to fix a surprisingly long list of bugs that are still found throughout Cyberpunk 2077.

The vast majority of these bugs are minor and only affect very small aspects of the overall game. We're talking things like slight animation glitches, specific audio mixing (those annoyingly quiet, and sometimes annoyingly loud TVs), and quest-related oddities.

Still, it's a mod worth installing when you start adding all of these fixes up — especially if you plan on starting a new playthrough.

This mod allows Johnny to appear in all of V's apartments, not just their starting home in the H10 megabuilding.

If you enjoy Johnny's company, this mod's good for immersion purposes. He'll lounge around the apartments, and add to the ambience by playing his guitar when V asks him to.

One of my favourite mods on PS5 so far, Weather Probability Rebalance does exactly what its name suggests, adjusting the chances of different weather patterns appearing as you carve out a life in Night City (and its surrounding wastelands).

For those who have already spent tens or even hundreds of hours playing Cyberpunk 2077, you may have noticed that the weather can be a bit... boring. The whole atmosphere of the city can change when it's raining, or when there's a sandstorm — but it can feel like it just doesn't happen often enough.

According to modder RMK_, the game's weather system is actually a little funky. In short, sunny weather can become 'stuck' under certain circumstances, and so this mod attempts to fix the problem.

As a result, adverse weather is much more common and lasts longer, allowing you to soak up the vibes.

A great mod for immersion purposes, Night City Interactions lets you go out drinking at various locations across the map — but the best part is that you can invite other characters, like Panam, Judy, River, and Kerry, to come along with you.

As a bonus, this mod also includes a Cyberpunk Edgerunners tour quest. As you may know, the anime features a number of backdrops that are based on actual locations from the game, and you can check these specific places out at your leisure.

Note that you need to enter V's H10 apartment (and then possibly exit) before this mod activates.

Three small mods that add just an extra touch of immersion to ripperdoc visits.

Instead of jumping straight to the cyberware menu upon talking to a ripper, V will actually sit down in the clinic's chair before undergoing surgery.

The Dogtown mod does the same for rippers in the Dogtown region of the map, while the Vic-specific mod uses Vic's existing animations from early in the game.

These are mods that, when used in conjunction with other immersion-focused mods, add up to a more detailed experience.

Another two mods that bring just a little more immersion to your time in Night City.

They let you sit down at the game's various bars and actually take a fully-animated drink. You can even select the kind of drink that you want from a dialogue menu.

What's more, the drinks give the same kind of temporary stat buffs that you get from consuming drinks in your inventory. A quick pre-gig bar crawl never hurt anyone!

Just like the Immersive Bartenders mods, this one lets you grab a fully-animated snack or drink from the numerous food vendors found across Night City.

Stat buffs are applied as if you were using items from your inventory, so it actually makes food stalls worth visiting if you're gearing up for some action.

This mod improves the readability of shards, which can be difficult to properly parse — especially if you're in a rush.

Basically, Readable Shards adjusts the text's formatting, making it slightly bigger and adding coloured names to the people who actually wrote the conversations in the first place.

This is a small mod but it can be a surprisingly big difference, particularly if you're a sucker for reading every bit of lore that you find.

A great little mod that adds a security camera system to NCARTS (metros).

By pressing left and right on the d-pad, you can switch to the cameras while you're riding the train, allowing you to view four new perspectives: two cameras shows the length of the carriage that you're on from either end, while the other two shows the outside of the metro from the front and back.

If you want to see more of Night City during your NCART travels, then this mod's an easy recommendation.

If you're absolutely sick of El Capitan giving you unreasonable time limits during his dynamic car-jacking gigs, then this mod's for you.

It simply increases said time limits by 25%, which usually equates to much easier missions. It also means that you can better enjoy the more combat-focused gigs without having to race ahead.

What are your favourite Cyberpunk 2077 mods on PS5? Hand out some recommendations in the comments section below.

Robert (or Rob if you're lazy) is an assistant editor of Push Square, and has been a fan of PlayStation since the 90s, when Tekken 2 introduced him to the incredible world of video games. He still takes his fighting games seriously, but RPGs are his true passion. The Witcher, Persona, Dragon Quest, Mass Effect, Final Fantasy, Trails, Tales — he's played 'em all. A little too much, some might say.

I haven't played it yet. But it's a real shame mods disable trophies (though I understand why) as that means I won't consider using these initially.

I've already platinumed the game and if you could prestige platinums I'd probably have done it about eight times over. So I'm super into the idea of mods to spice things up. "Undoubtedly, it would be very difficult to replicate the experience of consuming our game as intended because of technical limitations," says Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick has acknowledged the influx of AI-assisted game decompilations appearing online ahead of Rockstar Games releasing GTA 6 next week.

Recent months have seen a huge increase in the prevalence of vibe-coded AI-led recompilation projects. From Crash Team Racing to The Legend of Zelda: Link's Awakening, it seems that projects like this are now using AI more often than not – and while they might be releasing faster, the tech leaves a bad taste in the mouth for many.

This has put all eyes on GTA 6. With the absence of a GTA 6 PC port, there will be a number of players who can't access the game at launch – with many likely to double dip on the game by buying the console edition for launch and later picking up the PC version when it eventually comes to the platform. However, former Rockstar Games technical director Obbe Vermeij recently said he believes Rockstar may expedite its usual wait time of at least a year to get out in front of AI-powered attempts.

In a Take-Two investors' call, Zelnick is asked about the AI-powered recompilations, with the CEO responding, "this business has been largely immune to piracy concerns forever," and explaining: "Undoubtedly, it would be very difficult to replicate the experience of consuming our game as intended because of technical limitations."

However, Zelnick does note that with the influx of this new wave of recompilations, those piracy concerns are "going to become more of a challenge," saying that "we are utterly focused on enhancing our technical defenses and enhancing our legal activities appropriately."

Zelnick does acknowledge "every entertainment business that exists is subject to some element of piracy," but says: "I think it will be manageable, and we are focused on it."

Ultimately, I don't think a PC recompilation of GTA 6 will have any major effect on the game's financial performance. If it does happen, most are likely to abandon it in favor of the official PC port when that does drop, especially if it comes with GTA Online.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

GTA 6 being pirated is just "a fact of life," says CEO of Rockstar owner, and lawyers are ready if it becomes a problem.

#4072. NACON Releases REVO Range Of Xbox Controllers Designed For 'Every Gamer Style'

"Always Ready. Tailored Control. Pros' Arsenal."

NACON has announced today the availability of its REVO range of Xbox controllers, three officially licensed pads. The trio aims to accommodate the needs of every Xbox and PC player, because "every gamer has a style, every style has a controller."

The REVO X and REVO X MAX are available for purchase today, with the REVO X PRO arriving sometime in 2027. All three controllers are designed for different player styles, and so we've listed the price point and details for each pad. Here's how NACON described the REVO range:

"The new range has been designed to meet the specific needs of every type of player, from the casual gamer looking for the immediate efficiency of a "Plug-and-Play" controller, to the esports expert seeking deep customization."

The REVO controller is the embodiment of accessible and reliable performance. It is ideal for players looking for fluid control and flawless durability.

Announced for 2027, the REVO PRO is designed for the most demanding competitive players. It combines the best features of the range, including instant micro-switch triggers and programmable rear buttons, to offer optimized responsiveness and control for competition.

For players who demand complete customization, the REVO MAX offers advanced adjustment options to adapt the controller to their playstyle; these options are in addition to all the REVO features detailed above.

If you fancy picking up the REVO X or REVO X MAX, you can head to NACON's store directly via this link, or by the links embedded in each title above.

Though it didn't have a specific release date, Slitherine's refresh of the Warhammer-themed fantasy football game was scheduled for a full release in 2026. As of the announcement made at the Dominion Days showcase in Berlin, that's no longer the case.

"The game's history and the feedback received during the latest playtest have reinforced the team's belief that the game needs to be as polished as possible," Slitherine said, "as disappointing the fans is not an option."

That playtest is ongoing, and has just added an Arena mode where you try to make it through 10 matches in a row without losing a game or being forced to a draw more than twice. It's played in resurrection format, which means your team returns to its starting lineup at the end of each match, with no improvements or losses to carry over, so you better make sure your roster's a strong one from the off.

Slitherine also confirmed that Warhammer Blood Bowl's two new factions, the Tomb Kings and Bretonnians, will be added to the base game for free. Everyone who owns Blood Bowl 3 will be upgraded to Warhammer Blood Bowl without cost, and will get to keep access to any teams and cosmetics they've already paid for.

#4070. New TMNT: Splintered Fate Update Adds Even More Reasons To Play In Co-Op

Super Evil Megacorp has been steadily pumping out new content for its TMNT Hades-like, Splintered Fate, ever since launch, and today, the team has added a bunch of new reasons to embark on your roguelike runs in co-op.

The new Shell Squad Co-Op Update goes live today, and as its name suggests, it's all about the multiplayer fun. This free patch adds 24 new co-op powers, eight new co-op tools and eight new co-op masteries, so you can bring the heat to Shredder and the Rat King with even more skills when playing with friends.

The update also includes improved flame visuals, options for character swapping when playing co-op online or locally, and improved Lucky Dice communication.

Here are a few examples of the new powers and tools added in the update:

24x new co-op powers (3 per power tree). Examples: - Passing the Torch - The first player you touch while affected by Rapid Fire also gains its effects, for as long as you have Rapid Fire active. - Shared Warmth - When a player consumes a Splinter's Revive, heal all players. - Chain Reaction - Players' Specials have a chance to trigger a Chain Lightning, dealing Utrom damage per link.

8x new co-op tools (1 per power tree). Examples: - Bubble Trouble - Spawn a bubble on you and the farthest player. The bubble deals Water damage and Freezes enemies, and grants bonus Water damage to players. - Tether Beam - Tether to the closest player. Enemies caught in the beam will take Utrom damage every second. - Shadow Pact - Grant yourself and the closest player a Dark Shell. Each enemy defeated extends it.

8x new co-op masteries (1 per character). Examples: - Donatello - When using your Tool, the closest player becomes invulnerable. - Raphael - When any player lands a critical hit, they have a chance to Multi-crit instead. - Michelangelo - When using your Special, you and the closest player gain a Torrent Strike stack. - Leonardo - When activating your Special, the closest player gains Light Shell.

That's not all the news on the Splintered Fate front, either. The dev also announced its next paid cosmetics DLC: the Trench Coat Pack. Once again, it's another pretty self-explanatory one here, with all the Turtles (and the additional DLC characters) donning the team's iconic trench coats. This one is also available today, so there's no waiting around here, either!

#4069. GTA 6 Won't Have Any Last Minute Delays, as It's Officially Gone Gold

In case there was any doubt remaining, GTA 6 will definitely be making its debut on 19th November, 2026, with no risk of another delay of some kind.

That's because it's finally been confirmed the game has gone gold, which essentially means the open world action title is ready for release.

This comes via Take-Two's most recent earnings call, during which CEO Strauss Zelnick assured shareholders that GTA 6 had gone gold.

Separately, in an interview with IGN, he also says there are to be no further delays to the release. While that was unlikely given how close we are to the game's arrival, it's never a complete certainty until the software's actually out, so it's nice to have confirmation.

GTA 6 has been in the works for a very long time — at least the eight years since the launch of Red Dead Redemption 2 — so to hear the game is ready to roll out will be an exciting milestone for fans.

I've no doubt there will be additional patches and updates to install as Rockstar further irons out bugs and such.

For those who have pre-ordered the game on PS Store, you can begin pre-loading it starting today, and given the enormous file size, I'd recommend getting that download started as soon as you can.

Here's everything you need to do to get inside the Crimson Manor in Phantom Blade Zero

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Opening the Phantom Blade Zero Crimson Manor is a long and difficult process that you won't complete until you're very far into the game – basically, if you're reading this because you've just stumbled upon the manor under the Weeping Creek Valley Sha-Chi Tower, don’t worry about it for now!What makes it so complicated is that getting the necessary tongue key ties into several other side quests that will take you all over the game world, and the Crimson Manor quest itself links to an even greater over-arching side quest. But, to help you out, I've explained the entire process of getting inside the Crimson Manor – be aware that there are some story spoilers below!

To get inside the Crimson Manor, you need to get the Puppet's Tongue key by going through three hidden portal doors found across the game, all of which lead to the Three-Eyed Puppet (this is 'The Herald's Illusion' quest).

The arduous part is therefore finding those doors, especially since two of them are in far-flung regions of the game, so you need to make sure you have access to those regions first. To reach the Mandate Encampment, you need the Phantom Blade Zero Mandate Encampment Key. And to get to the Mountain of Imprisonment, you must have repaired the Illusory Pipa, which you can only do if you have found Myst in Pangzhen and thoroughly explored the Village of Lu, the Mandate Encampment, and Meigu Lake for the missing parts.

With all that in mind, here are the locations of the three secret doors:

When you go through the final door, interact with the Three-Eyed Puppet and it'll give you the necessary Puppet's Tongue, completing 'The Herald's Illusion' quest in the process, and finally giving you access to this mysterious subterranean mansion. The puppet also hands over its own Yin blue crystal eye and says that you need to find the Yang eye within the Crimson Manor, which is all for the 'Secrets at the Heart of the Lake' quest.

Anyway, fast travel to the Crimson Manor and interact with the lock to insert the tongue and open the door. Plunder the manor then head out the back and jump down the pit, carefully working your way to the bottom.

You'll be faced with a double boss fight against the Puppet Scavenger and Acolyte Hansui here. Neither are that tough, with the former's huge bulk making it slow and easy to hit and the latter being quite easy to overwhelm up close, so long as you dodge and block plenty of their ice attacks. Kill the pair and you'll get the Yang eye and Hansui's Frost Mask, thus finally completing the Crimson Manor quest!But now you've got the Yin and Yang crystal eyes and the 'Secrets at the Heart of the Lake' quest to wrap up. If you haven't already, you need to defeat the other three Acolyte boss fights found at scarecrows around the game – there's one in the Village of Lu, Pangzhen, and Lake Meigu – and take their masks to the Four Guardians' Mirror on the icy western side of Lake Meigu. This will take you to a special area where you'll eventually get to use those two crystal eyes, but only after you defeat the Blizzard Blademaster.

You've got to spend quite a lot of time in the Mandate Encampment for this quest, so make sure you grab Moji's House Key in Phantom Blade Zero while you're there. You'll also be facing a lot of bosses along the way, and it helps to have the best Phantom Blade Zero Accessories equipped.

#4067. Here's What Xbox Owners Need To Know About 'Moving To New Zealand' For GTA 6

So, it's finally almost time for GTA 6. You've probably preloaded the game on your Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S already, and now you're eagerly awaiting the official launch that takes place on November 19th.

However, there are more than a few whispers going around about the "New Zealand" trick — something we've seen time and time again over the past decade-plus on Xbox — and it looks set to have a big influence again with GTA 6.

But what is it, and most importantly could it get you banned? Let's take a look at the facts:

On this page: Here's What Xbox Owners Need To Know About 'Moving To New Zealand' For GTA 6

A game like GTA 6 obviously has a set release date of November 19th, but it lands at "midnight local time" depending on the region you're in. That means New Zealand ends up being the first region to get access, and their "midnight" corresponds to 3am PT / 6am ET / 11am GMT on November 18th.

Therefore, if people want to play the game as early as possible, they'll need to be in New Zealand - and the "New Zealand Trick" refers to changing your region in your console's settings, providing slightly early access to GTA 6.

There's always been a lot of chatter online about how Xbox doesn't really care about you "moving to New Zealand" to get around release times, but that's technically not the case. Xbox's terms and conditions specifically state that trying to "circumvent regional content restrictions" is prohibited, and this is mentioned a few times in documentation:

The official answer is yes - Xbox could take whatever kind of actions they wanted against an account that was found breaking the rules to play GTA 6 early on Xbox Series X and S. It could result in a warning, a suspension, a ban, or anything else they see fit.

You might also get away with it, as have the majority of people with many other games in the past, but it's still something you should only do at your own risk. We don't recommend breaking the rules just to play a game a few hours early, but we're also not naive enough to think that people won't be trying it come November 18th!

Something to also keep in mind with this is that spoilers will likely begin hitting the web from the New Zealand release time on November 18th (if not earlier). At that point, we expect all kinds of footage and screenshots to begin flooding social media, so you may want to have a bit of a digital detox until the 19th if you don't want to see anything.

Anyway, we know this is a hot topic, and feel free to share your thoughts about it in the comments below. The decision is up to you - but just know that you are running a risk by "moving to New Zealand", however small it might appear to be.

#4065. Persona 4 Revival Wasn't Meant to Be Part of Packed February 2027 Release Schedule

Persona 4 Revival was initially designed to launch for PS5 in the late summer months of this year, not the very crowded February 2027 release calendar it's now found itself in.

In an interview with 3DMGAME, chief producer Kazuhisa Wada shared the original plan was to launch the remake "as early as possible — we originally planned to release it about six months earlier, which would have been just in time for summer, but we ultimately couldn't make it that way".

The original Persona 4 often sparks memories of summer for players, as a large part of the game takes place during the season and includes trips to the beach and festivals specific to that part of the year. Putting the PS5 remake out during that same season would have made a lot of sense, but the Atlus executive claims the firm "couldn't make it that way".

It's not clear whether Wada is referring to development issues or a different problem that affected the release.

Either way, Persona 4 Revival now launches on 18th February 2027, a month full of other big PS5 releases. The delay to God of War Laufey gives everything else a touch more breathing room, but the schedule still looks like this:

As an RPG, its strongest competition is probably Fable, which releases just five days after Persona 4 Revival. The Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis remake should take up a lot of mindshare in the weeks before it, too.

We shall still play it in February, but getting to experience it again during those quieter summer months would have been bliss.

Liam grew up with a PlayStation controller in his hands and a love for Metal Gear Solid. Nowadays, he's found playing the latest and greatest PS5 games as well as supporting Derby County. That last detail is his downfall.

Maybe laying off people who know what they're doing is bad, actually.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

I don't know about you, but I'm not a huge fan of the way YouTube encourages everything becoming a video that's over an hour long and doesn't have a text version available. There's a recent video putting the original Pool of Radiance into the greater context of the history of CRPGs that's almost 10 hours long, and the odds of me watching more than 10% of it are perishingly low.

Fortunately for you, we're here to convert video to text for your edification, as with The Examined Game's comprehensive interview with Skyrim lead designer Bruce Nesmith. Asked how a game as successful as Skyrim came to be, Nesmith emphasized the importance of keeping the team together.

If I had an actual blueprint on how to do it, I would be one rich son of a bitch. A lot of it comes down to we had the same team that had worked on Oblivion. The studio had not really changed dramatically. So we were able to deal with institutional knowledge at a high level that had been retained, which allows us to not make mistakes and build on successes. That was definitely key to it.

I think also we gave a high priority to making sure that the world was full. There was nowhere that you went where there wasn't at least something fun to see if not something fun to do. And it and it can be just little things, it can be a little vignette on the side of the road. It doesn't have to be a huge big adventure, but the visual storytelling was fantastic.

I go back to that sense of freedom once again, but we accelerated that in Skyrim compared to Oblivion. It makes the world feel rich when there's a variety of experiences. The same experience over and over and over again doesn't cut it. So you have a wealth of enemy types, you've got a lot of different treasure types and loot types, you're allowed to pick everything up in the world.

I have to disagree with Nesmith on the characters, because memorable NPCs are one of Skyrim's weak spots—all those people with recycled voices and limited dialogue. But he's right that Skyrim feels full despite the absence of Ubisoft-style repeatable activities. At no point do you pick up a butterfly and get a notification that says "1/100 butterflies collected". The butterflies are just there, and you can grab them and turn them into potion ingredients if you want. Then while you're out harvesting ingredients you meet a thief or a dying orc or an NPC who points you to a sidequest, and you're off on a new journey. That's what Skyrim does well.

Nesmith goes on to say depth like that was made possible, "by having people who knew what they were doing and could hit the ground running. You didn't have to train people what it meant to make an Elder Scrolls game." Instead of laying off half the Oblivion team the moment it shipped, Bethesda kept them together. "If you look at the history of AAA studios that do sequels, you'll see that repeated," Nesmith continues. "You'll see the best game in a sequence frequently was able to maintain a particular percentage of the staff—was able to maintain a vision."
